properties.name: New York Transit Museum
properties.description: This is THE subway museum. New York City turned the unused Court Street Station into a horde of preserved MTA trains from the founding of the subway system until present.

properties.name: Coney Island Cyclone
properties.description: The Coney Island Cyclone was built in 1927 and due to its popularity has been replicated 8 times. The rollercoaster is famously intense, you will be thrown out of your seat, squished down into your seat, and thrown to the side of your seat over and over until your heart is racing.

properties.name: Wonder Wheel
properties.description: The Wonderwheel is the demented child of a rollercoaster and a ferris wheel, where your car swings freely in tracks. As gusts of seaside wind rock your carriage precariously, you will remember how much you value your life.

properties.name: The Henry Ford Museum of American Innovation
properties.description:
Henry Ford decided to buy all of American history and put it in the world's largest indoor-outdoor museum complex (12 acres indoors, 240 acres outdoors). It's an aerospace museum, a living history museum, automobile, railroad, and science museum,Including:

1.) All presidential limosines, including the ones John F. Kennedy and Ronald Reagan were shot in.
2.) The chair Abraham Lincoln was assassinated in.
3.) A 1:1 replica of Independence Hall.
4.) The Wright Brother's Bicycle shop where they developed the first airplane.
5.) Thomas Edison's Menlo Park Laboratory Complex.
6.) Rosa Park's bus.
7.) The homes and farms of Henry Ford, Thomas Edison, and Harvey Firstone.

properties.name: Detroit Institute of Arts
properties.description: See all the art Detroit purchased when it was the richest city in the world. There's also an entire Egyptian tomb and part of a European castle in here.

properties.name: Detroit Historical Museum
properties.description: Remember when Detroit was the 5th largest city in the United States of America and the richest city in the world? This museum sure does. Featuring assembly lines, a recreation of historical Detroit streets - including armored personnel carriers from all those times the Michigan National Guard had to quell riots.

properties.name: Motown Museum
properties.street: 2648 Berry Gordy Jr. Boulevard, 2648 W Grand Blvd, Detroit, MI 48208
properties.description: Music writer and producer Berry Gordy bought a bunch of houses, turned them into a music studio, and approached music production like a Detroit assembly line - turning artists into stars through rigorous trainining and quality control. This museum is where the Jackson 5, Stevie Wonder, Marvin Gaye, The Supremes, and the Four Tops got their start.

properties.name: Cranbrook Educational Community
properties.street: 380 Lone Pine Rd, Bloomfield Hills, MI 48304
properties.description: An Art Deco museum-garden complex created when Detroit was the richest city in the world. Featuring the Cranbrook Art Museum, the Cranbrook Institute of Science, and the Cranbrook House and Gardens.

properties.name: Gilmore Car Museum
properties.description: What's better than one building full of cars? 14 buildings full of cars set in an entire town built just for one car museum. It's 90 acres of cars.

properties.name: Sleeping bear Dunes National Lakeshore
properties.description: 35 miles of 450ft tall sand dunes next to the largest freshwater lakes in the world.

properties.name: Mackinac Island State Park
properties.description: Mackinac Island was the second national park after Yellowstone, but Michigan wanted it back. The state that is the heart of the American automotive industry banned cars on this island to preserve its beauty.

properties.name: S.S. City of Milwaukee
properties.description: The SS City of Milkwaukee is the last railroad ferry on the Great Lakes. It's also a museum, hotel, and haunted house depending on the time of year. The USCGC Acacia is also docked as a museum ship.

properties.name: S.S. Milwaukee Clipper
properties.description: It's museum passenger/car ferry ship built in 1904 and modernized in the 1950s. The resulting ship feels uniquely like a cross between an insane-asylum and a bus.

properties.name: Gerald R. Ford Presidential Museum
properties.street: 303 Pearl St NW, Grand Rapids, MI 49504
properties.description: Come see the Gerald R. Ford Presidential Museum where you can learn that President Gerald Ford did nothing wrong (in their opinion).

properties.name: Pictured Rocks National Lakeshore
properties.description: It's fancy rocks, waterfalls, sand dunes, and shipwrecks on the world's largest freshwater lake by surface area. The lake is 45F all year round, so enjoy the breeze - but don't go swimming.

properties.name: Top-of-the-Lake Snowmobile Museum
properties.description: Snowmobiles are awesome. I like them. The Upper Peninsula of Michigan is one of the snowiest location in the United States, and the snowmobile trails in the region reflect that.

properties.name: Porcupine Mountains Wilderness State Park
properties.description: Waterfalls, dynamic cliffs, and a lake in the sky (Lake of the Clouds) in this stunning state park.

properties.name: Quincy Mine
properties.description: A Michigan Upper Peninsula Copper mine that remains frightfully cold year round. Part of the Keweenaw National Historical Park.

properties.name: SS Valley Camp
properties.street: 501 E Water St, Sault Ste. Marie, MI 49783
properties.description: Come see a 1917 Great Lakes Freighter in its native habitat: next to a massive set of locks between Lake Superior and Lake Huron. The museum is in the actual cargo hold - a rarity among museum ships in the Great Lakes.

properties.name: U.S.S. Edson
properties.description: The USS Edson is a 1958 Forrest-Sharman class destroyer. U.S. Navy veteran volunteers tend to mull about on deck. Interestingly, this ship museum lets you wander around the engine room with very little restrictions.

properties.name: Air Zoo
properties.description: The Air Zoo is a combined children's amusement park and aerospace museum. The flight simulators let you do barrel rolls and loops and I highly recommend them. Uniquely, the air zoo has a Curtiss Ascender, F-117 Nighthawk, SR-71B Blackbird

properties.name: Sloan Museum
properties.description: 80,000 people used to work in 37 General Motors Automotive Factories in Flint, Michigan. Today that number is less than 8000. All the while General Motors placed its prototypes and successes in this local museum named after the CEO that took General Motors to its zenith when it held 50% market share in the U.S. auto market.

properties.name: USS Silversides Submarine Museum
properties.description: A World War Two Gato-class submarine that sunk 23 enemy ships in the Pacific Theater is now available for tour in Muskegon, Michigan - a place that is most definitely not the ocean.

properties.name: Icebreaker Mackinaw Maritime Museum
properties.street: 131 S Huron Ave, Mackinaw City, MI 49701
properties.description: The Great Lakes freeze during the winter, but ships still need to move. The USCGC Mackinaw is a 1944 icebreaker designed specifically for Great Lakes service to extend the shipping season. As a result it looks unique compared to other icebreakers.

properties.name: Tahquamenon Falls State Park
properties.description: Copper-colored 50ft waterfalls in the rocky wilderness of the Upper Peninsula of Michigan.

properties.name: National Museum of the Great Lakes
properties.description: The National Museum of the Great Lakes features the SS Colonel James M. Schoonmaker, a 1911 Great Lakes iron ore freighter. Despite its nautical appearances, the crew quarters on the stern is lavishly decorated like a Victorian mansion.

properties.name: Rutherford B. Hayes Presidential Library and Museums
properties.description: It's called the Rutherford B. Hayes Presidential Library and Museum, but it should be more accurately titled the "Medal of Honor Recipient Webb C. Hayes Museum, featuring my dad who did nothing wrong: President Rutherford B. Hayes".

properties.name: Cedar Point
properties.description: 19 World class rollercoasters on the eleventh largest freshwater lake in the world. Winner of Best Amusement Park In The World for 16 consecutive years. Featuring multiple rollercoasters that have all been ranked as best in the world at the time of their opening.

properties.name: National Museum of the United States Air Force
properties.description: This is THE military aviation museum. The largest military aviation museum in the world with 360 aircraft and missiles on display. Come see presidential aircraft, nuclear missiles and bombs, stealth fighters and bombers, spy satellites, experimental aircraft, and friendly recruiters who would like you to join the United States Air Force. Admission is free.

properties.name: Cincinnati Museum Center
properties.description: The train station that was the basis for DC's Hall of Justice is now a museum center. Somehow there is an entire steamboat (complete with historical waterfront), cave, ice cave, and forest in the basement. Also dinosaurs, mummies, and astronauts. It is just as glorious as it sounds.

properties.name: Columbus Zoo and Aquarium
properties.description: Jack Hanna's legendary zoo with 800 species of animals, including manatees, lions, leopards, tigers, elephants, lynxes, sea lions and seals, cheetahs, sea turtles, penguins, koalas, moose, river otters, pallas cats, polar bears, etc. There's also two rollercoasters and an outstanding waterpark built into the zoo.

properties.name: Cuyahoga Valley National Park
properties.description: Cuyahoga Valley National park doesn't look like much until you peer into the 65ft deep rocky ravine filled with 100 waterfalls. Brandywine Falls by itself is a stunning attraction that is well worth a look.

properties.name: Wordens Ledges
properties.street: Wordens Ledges Loop Trail, Hinckley, OH 44233
properties.description: Terrifying century old rock visiages carved into the face of a cliff deep in the woods. I genuinely felt I was going to get murdered despite being in the safe suburbs of Cleveland.

properties.name: Serpent Mound
properties.description: Native Americans built a giant snake shaped mound on top of a hill more than 2000 years ago. It's still there snaking in the woods.

properties.name: Warren G. Harding Presidential Library and Museum
properties.description: President Warren G. Harding promised to "Return to Normalcy" and "Make America Great Again" following American overseas interventionism, enforced political correctness, percieved weakness on immigration, and a plague. A favorite of newspaper reporters due owning his own newspaper where the country could hear his thoughts, Harding also presided over a corrupt cabinet, womanized, then died of a heart attack after being strained from touring the country for massive rallies. This is his museum and tomb.

properties.name: McKinley Presidential Library and Museum
properties.street: 800 Mc Kinley Monument Dr NW, Canton, OH 44708
properties.description: President William McKinley followed the proud presidential tradition of being from Ohio and getting shot - which means his tomb is very nice because the nation was very sad. For some reason there's also dinosaurs in his museum.

properties.name: The Cleveland Museum of Art
properties.description: Cleveland used to be rich, bought a lot of nice art, and made the art museum free forever. Yes, they have the Etruscan Boar Vessel and the Majapahit piggy bank.

properties.name: Kings Island
properties.description: The Eiffel Tower, 15 rollercoasters, including a homemade 7361ft ride through the woods. Kings Island is one of the world's greatest amusement parks which revived the public's interest in rollercoasters following the decline of the amusement industry in the 1970s.

properties.name: Hocking Hills State Park
properties.description: Caves and waterfalls, waterfalls in caves, rock overhangs, and gentle hikes. It's like Ohio is trying to trick you into thinking it's a nice place to be.

properties.name: Early Television Museum
properties.description: Did you know you can make a television screen out of a single lightbulb and a spinning disc with holes in it? Learn about the wacky frontier of television when television stations went to bed for the evening, and the British could still manufacture electronics.

properties.name: Trap History Museum
properties.description: 4000 traps of all types and historical periods located next to a public safety equipment supplier to remind them of the consequences should they fail. Come see 20ft giant bear trap that might be our only protection against Godzilla. Tours by appointment only - please call ahead of time.

properties.name: Age of Steam Roundhouse
properties.description: You know how at most railroad museums the trains just sit there and don't do anything? The trains at the Age of Steam Roundhouse actually still run and you can ride in them. They also have a compressed air powered locomotive.

properties.name: The Troll Hole Museum
properties.description: Are you feeling too sane? Why not learn about trolls, see cellebrities turned into rolls, troll based cinema, and find out if Santa is really a troll. It's the world's largest troll collection.

properties.name: Great Lakes Science Center
properties.description: Featuring the NASA Glenn Visitor Center (with an actual Apollo capsule used for Skylab) and the Great Lakes Freighter William G Mather. The rest of the stuff is for kids.

properties.name: Rock and Roll Hall of Fame
properties.description: Memorabilia from history's greatest modern music performers. Located in Cleveland because some radio DJ here created the phrase ''Rock and Roll".

properties.name: Jungle Jims International Market Eastgate
properties.description: Jungle Jims International Market literally has everything. This is the infinite IKEA of grocery stores. Yes there is a movie theater that only shows propaganda promoting the store that you are already in. Yes there is a bar. Yes there is a card game shop.

properties.name: American Sign Museum
properties.description: All the good signs all in a former sign factory. This museum fulfills mankind's truest desire to look at pretty flashing lights in funny shapes.

properties.name: Mansfield Memorial Museum
properties.description: Home of Elektro - one of the first ever robots displayed at the 1939 New Yorks's World Fair. Elektro could walk, talk, smoke a cigarette, blow a balloon, move its arms and fingers, and be enslaved by humanity (something that we will surely never come to regret). This museum isn't the best museum, I just really like Elektro.

properties.name: Crystal Cave
properties.description: Ever wanted to stand in a cave surrounded by crystals like some kind of ancient enchanter? Now you can! There's another cave across the street if you are waiting for the ferry to take you back to the mainland.

properties.name: Ohio Caverns
properties.description: Most caves are all the same color of rock, the caves at Ohio caverns are multi-colored and still wet and drippy. Considering how flat everything is in the area this is the most exciting geological feature for nearly 100 miles in every direction. Breathe it in.

properties.name: Camden Park
properties.description: A scooby-doo esque run-down amusement park built on a native American burial ground. The back seat of the Big Dipper rollercoaster was one of the few times I felt close to death. A fun time for the whole family.

properties.name: New River Gorge National Park and Preserve
properties.description: A deep river gorge in Appalachia with whitewater rafting and a bridge that is impossibly large to comprehend until you see it in person. When you see the wispy clouds moving through gorge and over the mountaintops you'll understand why this had to be made into a national park.

properties.name: The Greenbrier
properties.street: 101 W Main St, White Sulphur Springs, WV 24986
properties.description: Congress built a bunker to protect itself from nuclear war under a luxury hotel. As of this moment this is the only United State continuity of government complex availible for tour, as Raven Rock Mountain Complex, Mount Weather Emergency Operations Center, and Warrenton Training Center continue to be in use to this day.

properties.name: Seneca Rocks
properties.description: Seneca Rocks are a concerningly thin scenic rock crag rising 900ft above the Monongahela National Forest. There's a 2-hour hike to an observation deck at the top that provides a good view of the surrounding area.

properties.name: West Virginia State Museum
properties.street: Building 9, 1900 Kanawha Blvd E #435, Charleston, WV 25305
properties.description: Most state museums try to be inoffensive and lack coherent vision. By comparison, the West Virginia state museum offers a compelling walk through the state's history where visitors quite literally advance through time as they move through the exam. See how the state developed from woodland, to native history, to arrival of European settlers, to the U.S. Civil War, to mining and the present.

properties.name: Cathedral Falls
properties.description: Cathedrals falls is tucked away next to a very unsafe to drive on feeling highway. However, you can walk right up to the 60ft tall waterfall, and the cliffs are shaped in such a way they arch over your head like the roof of a cathedral. Pictures do not do it justice.

properties.name: Beckley Exhibition Coal Mine
properties.description: Beckley Exhibition Coal Mine opened in 1889, ceased operations in 1953, and became the world's first public museum entirely dedicated to coal mining in 1962. Yes, you can go into the coal mine, and you get there in a tiny train.

properties.name: Lost World Caverns
properties.description: A cavern with formations so fancy they are registered as a National Natural Landmark. There's a half mile loop of walking worth to do. The caverns are so spacious that self-guided tours are available.

properties.name: Isle Royale National Park
properties.description: The largest island of the largest freshwater lake in the world by surface area. 45 miles of jagged granite shores, abandoned copper mines, and untouched wilderness. Only accessible by boat or aircraft - there are no vehicles allowed on the island, so I hope you love hiking.

properties.name: Museum of Science and Industry
properties.street: 5700 S DuSable Lake Shore Dr, Chicago, IL 60637
properties.description: A permanent structure from the 1893 World's Columbian Exposition houses a stainless-steel passenger train, a german U-boat, space capsules, an extensive model railroad, a mockup of old chicago streets, and a mockup coal mine.

properties.name: Field Museum
properties.description:
The Field Museum of Natural History features multiple sections each expansive and detailed enough to be museums in their own right. Set aside an entire day for the Field Museum, it is mind-bogglingly extensive. These sections include but are not limited to:
1.) Fossils in dioramas organized by era, with funny little extinction event placards breaking up the sections as you walk through them.There is a nearly complete fossil of a T-Rex.
2.) Artifacts and houses from the pacific islands collected by a rich guy who was determined to capture how life was lived before Europeans showed up.
3.) a three story replica of an egyptian tomb complete with mummies.

properties.name: The Art Institute of Chicago
properties.description: 300,000 paintings seems like a reasonable number of paintings to justify an art museum. Occupying a building from the 1893 World's Columbian Exposition, the Art Institute of Chicago has got the painting made of a bunch of dots and the one with the farmers and the pitchfork.

properties.name: Shedd Aquarium
properties.street: 1200 S DuSable Lake Shore Dr, Chicago, IL 60605
properties.description: Having an Aquarium full of piranhas, electric eels, sea turtles, sharks, dolpins, belugas, sea otters, sea lions, and penguins is made all the more impressive by the fact that this aquarium is 700 miles from the ocean.

properties.name: Chicago History Museum
properties.description: If you ever dreamed of seeing Chicago burning, this museum has a diorama to help you visualize it. Chicago burned to the ground in 1871 and just can't seem to let it go. This museum also features some antique cars from the elevated rail network.

properties.name: Institute for the Study of Ancient Cultures Museum
properties.description: Have you ever said: "Wow, I sure wish someone other than the British took the ancient treasures of the middle east". Well, you're in luck.

properties.name: Par King Skill Golf
properties.description: This is the mini-golf course from cartoons in real life. It's got golf loopdeloop, golf rollercoaster, golf statute of liberty, golf roulette wheel, and golf taking the stairs at Sears Tower.

properties.name: Illinois Railway Museum
properties.description: This is THE train museum in the USA. The largest railroad museum in the United States. 11 Storage barns on an 80 acre campus with over 200 trains and 500 pieces of rolling stock in total. Trains, interurbans, trolleys, buses, you name it.

properties.name: Caterpillar Visitors Center
properties.description: Remember the yellow construction equipment toys you played with as a kid? This is where the actual equipment is made. Come and see all of it at the Caterpillar Visitors Center. Come on, you know you've always wanted to sit in the cab of a 2-story dump truck.

properties.name: Abraham Lincoln Presidential Library and Museum
properties.description: Illinois loves Abraham Lincoln so much they made the official state slogan "Land of Lincoln" and forgot they voted for Stephen Douglas for Senator instead. This museum covers everything about Abraham Lincoln, including a diorama of the part of his life where he went to the theater. Presidential security has come a long way since Lincoln, with only 6 other sitting or former Presidents being shot, representing 22% of all Presidents since Lincoln. Progress.

properties.name: Cahokia Mounds State Historic Site
properties.description: 80 Earthen mounds with some standing over 100ft tall mark the site of a pre-Columbian city where 20,000 people once lived in 1100AD. The largest pre-Columbian earthen Construction in the United States and a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Cahokia was abandoned long before European settlers arrived and gave nearby St. Louis the nickname "Mound City".

properties.name: Garden of the Gods Recreation Area
properties.description: The observation trail in the Garden of the Gods Recreation Area of Shawnee National Forest leads to a cliff with sandstone rock formations and panoramnic views of the surrounding area. There's also other interesting hiking trails in the area.

properties.name: Cave In Rock State Park
properties.street: 1 New State Park Rd, Cave-In-Rock, IL 62919
properties.description: A 55ft tall keyhole shaped cave on the limestone bluffs of the Ohio River. Cave-In-Rock was the first State Park of Illinois which should give you an idea that people have always thought it was pretty neat.

properties.name: Little Grand Canyon - Shawnee National Forest
properties.description: Spiderweb like limestone formations and seasonal waterfalls in this canyon in Shawnee National Forest. It's a 2.9 mile hike, so expect to take 3-4 hours.

properties.name: Starved Rock State Park
properties.description: Canyons, waterfalls, and cliffs that look much bigger in person than they do in photos all at this state park which boasts very easy to do hikes.

properties.name: PEZ Visitor Center
properties.description: PEZ history, PEZ Trivia, PEZ factory, PEZ merchandise, the PEZ motorcycle, and the world's largest PEZ dispenser. The ultimate PEZ collection at the PEZ factory.

properties.name: Submarine Force Library and Museum
properties.description: Connecticut has long been home to the United States' Submarine Force since the Electric Boat Company set up their modern facility in Groton in 1931. Tour the USS Nautilus - the world's first nuclear submarine. The museum also features a replica of the Turtle, a WW2 Kairyu-class Japanese midget submarine, the X-1 American Midget Submarine

properties.name: Mystic Seaport Museum
properties.description: This is THE whaling museum. It's not just a whaling ship museum, it's an entire whaling industry living-history town.  Featuring the Charles W. Morgan- the last wooden sailing ship, along with 14 other historic ships, and 39 historic buildings.

properties.name: Mystic Aquarium
properties.description: Listen, they have Japanese Spider Crabs. There's belugas and sea lions too if you're into that.

properties.name: Danbury Railway Museum
properties.description: A fine collection of self-propelled 1950s interurban cars, including a Mack Truck railbus. Yes you can just wander around inside them as they sit decaying, and it is beautiful.

properties.name: Connecticut Trolley Museum
properties.description: Your admission includes unlimited rides on the trolleys through the the 2.4 mile heritage railroad.

properties.name: Shoreline Trolley Museum
properties.description: Trolleys in a swamp - the opposite of their natural habitat. 100 streetcars at the United State's oldest operating trolley museum - including the oldest operating trolley in the United States. However, you only get to tour the trolley barns briefly after a mandatory 1.5 mile scenic trolley ride through the marsh.

properties.name: Magnolia Wilds
properties.description: You can swim with otters and pet capybaras - for a hefty price. To simplify: otters are slippery, and capybaras feel like petting a broom. There, saved you $300.00.

properties.name: Louisiana Old Governors Mansion
properties.description: Governor Huey Long commissioned a governor's mansion that was identical to the whitehouse to bolster his presidential ambitions. Long was assassinated in 1936, but the mansion remains as a Louisiana version of the highest office on Earth.

properties.name: National WWII Museum
properties.description: World War Two: The Museum. If you need to get people as interested in World War II as you are - this is the place.

properties.name: Albacore Park
properties.description: The USS Albacore was the first U.S. submarine designed for purely underwater performance, utilizing a teardrop hall and high tensile steel that became the standard worldwide. The submarine now rests entirely on dry land nearby the naval shipyard where she was built.

properties.name: Mt. Washington State Park
properties.street: 1598 Mt Washington Auto Rd, MOUNT WASHINGTON, NH 03589
properties.description: Mt. Washington is the place on earth with the highest recorded wind speed of 231 mph. Despite being the windiest place on earth, you can drive your car to the top because this is America.

properties.name: Mount Washington Cog Railway
properties.description: The "Railway to the Moon". The second steepest rack-railway in the world goes to the top of the windiest mountain in the world. Tickets are expensive, and most of the cool steam locomotives have been replaced with diesels - but the few steam engines that remain are really really cool. Come on, you know you want to take a train up a mountain.

properties.name: Franconia Notch State Park
properties.street: Flume Gorge Visitor Center, 852 Daniel Webster Hwy, Lincoln, NH 03251
properties.description: Franconia Notch used to be home of New Hampshire's Old Man of The Mountain, a mountain face that looked like a human face profile. However, that collapsed. The waterfalls and flume gorge are still well worth a visit.

properties.name: Shelburne Museum
properties.description: The heiress to the US Sugar monopoly decided to spend all her money collecting everything. She hauled a steamship and lighthouse up a mountain, and relocated her New York Apartment. Come see the museum of museums, stuffed animals, carved circus creatures, guns, art, carriages, and creepy dolls - all at the Shelburne Museum.

properties.name: Ben and Jerrys Factory
properties.description: The promised land where Ben and Jerrys ice cream is made. The ice cream tastes better here because it is fresh, and the factory tour is amazing.

properties.name: Seashore Trolley Museum
properties.description: This is THE trolley museum. The largest electric railway museum in the world with over 250 mass transit vehicles. The volunteers at the Seashore Trolley museum have been hoarding more buses, trolleys, and trains in the woods than they can realistically restore. Have you ever wanted to see literal piles of buses and trolleys? This is the place.

properties.name: Acadia National Park
properties.description: Acadia National Park covers Mt. Desert Island, a scenic granite island with beautiful mountains and lakes - and only one beach. Come see a pair of mountains called The Bubbles which for some reason the national park service is in denial of what they really look like. The hiking here is gorgeous, fun, and relatively easy. Due to its popularity, you will need reservations to go up Mt. Cadillac by car.

properties.name: Island Cruises Bass Harbor
properties.street: 12 Little Island Way, Bass Harbor, ME 04653
properties.description: A lobster boat has been converted into a tourist cruise vessel and will show you all the best islands nearby Acadia while regalling you with local history. The views are stunning, the sealife is abundant , and they will pull up a lobster trap so you can see how it's done.

properties.name: Nervous Nellies Jams and Jellies
properties.description: Terrifying scrap folk art in the foggy Maine woods. That may be downplaying it, the artist built an entire facade town complete with tower, castle, church, saloon, jail, inn, and much much more. The jam is pretty good too.

properties.name: Fort Knox and Penobscot Narrows Observatory
properties.description: This place definitely feels haunted. Damp granite fortifications with a commanding view of the Penobscot narrows make Fort Knox well worth visiting.  Additionally, there is an observatory on the nearby bridge that gives a good view of all of Maine.

properties.name: Grafton Notch State Park
properties.description: Dramatic swooshing waterfalls, boulder covered hiking trails,  and imposing granite mountains in the backwoods of Maine. Screw Auger Falls in particular looks like it was carved out of a fantasy novel.

properties.name: Baxter State Park
properties.description: Baxter State Park is home of Mt. Katahdin, the tallest mountain in Maine (5,267ft). The mountains in the park are especially prominent, and the nearby lakes just make them look taller.

properties.name: Funtown Splashtown USA
properties.description: An amusement park set in the mystical woods of Maine. Featuring a psychdellic indoor scrambler, a fast log flume where guests can ambush riders with water cannons, and a rollercoaster deep in the forest.

properties.name: Story Land
properties.description: This children's amusement park in the is a vivid fever dream and is near no major cities. Despite being aimed at children, there is a surprisingly intense dinosaur themed wooden rollercoaster here. The only amusement park that I know of scored with a unique soundtrack by a composer. I turned a corner here and was confronted by animatronic singing bamboo.

properties.name: Indiana Dunes National Park
properties.description: Next to Chicago lays massive sand dunes on the shores of the world's largest freshwater lake system.

properties.name: Albanese Candy Factory Store
properties.description: The source of the most delicious gummy candy in the world.

properties.name: Indiana Beach
properties.street: 5224 E Indiana Beach Rd, Monticello, IN 47960
properties.description: An Americana themed amusement park tightly packed on top of itself on a pier in the middle of a lake in the middle of Indiana. Notable features include a wooden rollercoaster stuffed into the corpse of a dark ride, a wooden rollercoaster built over the lake itself, and a wooden rollercoaster built over the rest of the park. Their slogan is "There's More Than Corn In Indiana".

properties.name: Minnetrista Museum and Gardens
properties.description: Home of the Bob Ross Experience. Paint your own happy little trees in Bob Ross's workshop. Oh and I guess there's some beautiful gardens here too.

properties.name: Holiday World And Splashin Safari
properties.street: 452 E Christmas Blvd, Santa Claus, IN 47579
properties.description: Did you know Edgar Allen Poe's poem 'The Raven' has its own rollercoaster themed after it? Holiday World is an amusement park themed to American holidays, oddly enough featuring the best waterpark in the United States. The Thanksgiving rollercoaster named The Voyage is renowend as one of the best rollercoasters ever built.

properties.name: International Monster Truck Museum and Hall of Fame
properties.description: Every lifted truck tries to imitate the glory of a Monster Truck but is a pale comparison. Come see the trucks that can do backflips and crush European sedans at the International Monster Truck Museum and Hall of Fame.

properties.name: RV/MH Hall of Fame
properties.description: 85% of All North American RVs are built in Elkhart Indiana and is known as the "RV Capital of the World". This hall of fame honors the legends of the motoring home industry and documents the development of the RV.

properties.name: Studebaker National Museum
properties.description: You know those stylish cars from the 1950s? These are those cars. Studebaker was unique in that it was a carriage manufacturer that transitioned to automotive and lasted until 1968. Studebakers featured bolder styling compared to contemporary car manufacturers. This museum also has Abraham Lincoln's carriage from the night he got assassinated.

properties.name: Auburn Cord Duesenberg Automobile Museum
properties.description: Auburn Automobile and Duesenberg were luxury American car manufacuters that went bankrupt during the Great Depression. See a 1920s Art Deco automotive showroom filled with luxury vehicles housed in Auburn's headquarters as well as 120 vehicles curated for their signifigance. Literally right next to this outstanding automotive museum is the National Auto and Truck Museum so yeah, you're gonna see cars.

properties.name: National Auto and Truck Musem
properties.street: 1000 Gordon M Buehrig Pl, Auburn, IN 46706
properties.description: What's better than 120 vehicles at the nearby Auburn Cord Duesenberg Automobile Museum? 190+ classic cars, vintage trucks, rare prototypes including the GM Futurliner, and 6000+ model toy cars.

properties.name: Marengo Cave
properties.description: It's big, it's long, it's a mile of cave in Indiana. A U.S. National Natural Landmark offering two separate hour-long tours.

properties.name: West Baden Springs Hotel
properties.street: 8538 W Baden Ave, West Baden Springs, IN 47469
properties.description: "Indiana's Monte Carlo" - seriously that's what the submission for the National Register of Historical Places says -opened with the largest dome in the world in 1902 and is one of America's few remaining Grand Hotels. The trolley at the hotel takes you straight to the French Lick Casino to spend your hard earned social security checks.

properties.name: Turkey Run State Park
properties.description: Narrow sandstone canyons that feel like the arches of a subway tunnel with waterfalls in the middle. There's also rocky cliffs facing the river.

properties.name: Bluespring Caverns Park
properties.street: 1459 Blue Springs Cavern Rd, Bedford, IN 47421
properties.description: Kayak or boat on the world's largest navigable underground river (1-3 hour tour) at Bluespring Cavern in Indiana. Bet kayaking on an underground river in Indiana wasn't on your bucket list.

properties.name: Indianapolis Motor Speedway Museum
properties.description: 400,000 people per year attend the Indianapolis Motor Speedway for the Indianapolis 500 . This museum is set in the heart of the racetrack that is the highest capacity sports venue in the world. Come and see the cars that have won the the top event in American open-wheel car racing.

properties.name: USS LST-325
properties.description: Landing Ship Tanks beach themselves to allow rapid unloading of invading forces via the bow doors, and require a shallow draft with high cargo capacity. LST-325 particpated in the Normandy Landings, and is the sole remaining operational LST in the United States.

properties.name: Squire Boone Caverns
properties.street: 100 Squire Boone Rd SW, Mauckport, IN 47142
properties.description: A cave full of rushing water and underground waterfalls that disappears into a sinkhole. The stream that powers the gristle mill on the surface is the same as underground.

properties.name: Indiana Caverns
properties.street: 1267 Green Acres Dr SW, Corydon, IN 47112
properties.description: A 40ft underground waterfall bursting through the ceiling and a underground riverboat ride will really make you feel like you descended to the underworld in Indiana. This cavern is notable for the numerous ice-age fossils present.

properties.name: National Railroad Museum
properties.description: It's not the biggest railroad museum, however the National Railroad Museum possesses  some notably locomotives, such as General Motors Aerotrain, Union Pacific Railroad Big Boy, British Rail A4 used by Supreme Allied Commander Dwight Eisenhower, and a GG1.

properties.name: Bay Beach Amusement Park
properties.street: 1313 Bay Beach Rd, Green Bay, WI 54302
properties.description: The people of Green Bay love Green Bay so much that their municipal government built an affordable amusement park just for the people of Green Bay. To top is off, Bay Beach Park relocated Elvis's favorite rollercoaster - the Zippin Pippin from Memphis to Green Bay.

properties.name: SS Meteor Maritime Museum
properties.description: The whaleback was a unique ship hull design optimized for maximum cargo and hydrodynamic efficiency by removing above-water area for wind and wave resistance. The SS Meteor is the last of its kind and is a goofy looking ship all around.

properties.name: Pattison State Park
properties.description: Pattison State Park is home to the 165ft tall Big Manitou Falls and the much less impressive 50ft Little Manitou Falls. The woods of Wisconsin don't get more scenic than this.

properties.name: Apostle Islands National Lakeshore
properties.description: Apostle Island National Lakeshore consisted of fantasy-like sandstone cliffs and sea caves on the edge of the largest freshwater lake in the world. The only problem is that most of the park is on islands, so you need a ocean-going kayak or to take a tour boat to really get a good look at any of it.

properties.name: Willow River State Park
properties.description: Willow River State Park is home to Willow Falls, a roaring waterfall in a 200ft deep gorge with dramatic overhangs.

properties.name: Mill Bluff State Park
properties.description: Sea stacks from ancient glacial lakes are now extremely out of place and make for good scenic hiking at Mill Bluff State Park.

properties.name: The House On The Rock
properties.description: Have you ever wanted to experience an architectural version of a Salvador Dali painting? The House On The Rock is built on top of a steep rock, features Japanese gardens, a larger than life sized whale fighting a kraken, and a doll carousel inside. It is very difficult to describe the contents of this location because the contents are deliberately surreal.

properties.name: The Mining and Rollo Jamison Museums
properties.description: Where else can you tour a lead mine?

properties.name: Little Amerricka Amusement Park
properties.description: It's 1950s decorations with 1950s safety sensitibilities at this classic park. Little Amerricka is home to a 3 mile long miniature railway, a rollercoaster with no seatbelts, a parachute tower, and a rollercoaster where you get inside the torture shoebox to bump your head.

properties.name: EAA Aviation Museum
properties.description: The Experimental Aircraft Association has their own museum, featuring 200+ wacky and unique aircraft like the 1938 Bugatti Model 100 Racer, A rebuilt 1949 Tyler Aerocar, and Spaceship 1. EAA is right next to the annual weeklong EAA AirVenture Oshkosh event, the world's largest airshow.

properties.name: Harley-Davidson Museum
properties.description: See over 450 motorcycles and trace the history of the legendary Harley-Davidson motorcycle company, up to and including when they stopped being affordable and cool.

properties.name: Wisconsin Maritime Museum
properties.description: There's a mockup of an entire shipyard inside of the museum, and the USS Cobia, a WW2 Gato-class submarine docked outside.

properties.name: Bass Pro Shops Pyramid
properties.description: The ancient Egyptian city of Memphis was known for its pyramid where they kept their honored treasures. So too the American city of Memphis, Tennessee keep their treasures in their 312 foot pyramid. It's a hotel, bar, bowling alley, observation deck, waterfowl hunting museum, and largest Bass Pro Shop in the world.

properties.name: Graceland
properties.description: Everything Elvis, including his airplanes, tacky 70s mansion, and automobiles. Elvis Presley was the best selling music artist in history during his lifetime, and pioneered modern rock-and-roll as a genre. Even today, Elvis impersonators make their livings by pretending to be The King.

properties.name: National Civil Rights Museum
properties.description: Martin Luther King was shot here, his death inspired riots nationwide in 1968. This museum has a bus that you can get kicked out of your seat in, a bus that you can be set on fire in for trying to get people the right to vote, a lunch counter you can be harassed at for daring to order food, and a jail to get locked up in for getting out of line. All in all, the complete American Civil Rights experience.

properties.name: USS Cairo Gunboat and Museum
properties.description: The USS Cairo was a union ironclad river gunboat during the US Civil War and was the first ship to ever be sunk by a remotely detonated mine. The wreck was found, excavated, and new parts put onto the outside so that you can get a feel for its construction. The USS Cairo is the only Civil War era river gunboat available for tour in existence.

properties.name: Vicksburg National Military Park
properties.description: The 47-day Siege of Vicksburg marked the turning point of the U.S. Civil War in the Union's favor. 30,000 Confederate soldiers were captured, and the Mississippi river came under the complete control of Union forces - cutting the Confederacy in two. Vicksburg National military Park features 20 miles of trenches and earthworks along the siege lines and offers an outstanding view of the Mississippi river.

properties.name: Lower Mississippi River Museum
properties.description: See the M/V Mississippi IV, a United States Army Corp of Engineers vessel used for towing, river inspections, and public meetings. There's also various history about the Mississippi River and an outdoor scale flood model.

properties.name: Red Bluff Mississippi
properties.description: This colorful cliff keeps swallowing the nearby highway. The wreckage of cars and trains lay at the bottom near well marked trails.

properties.name: INFINITY Science Center
properties.description: The Mississippi Rocket Test Stand at nearby Stennis Space Center doesn't do public tours, but they gave this place a Saturn V Booster and Apollo 4 Command Capsule.

properties.name: Jefferson Davis Presidential Library and Museum
properties.description: It's like the evil universe version of a United State Presidential Library where President of the Confederate States of America Jefferson Davis is honored at this museum run by the state of Mississippi. Their favorite words to use there are "Heritage", "Resilience", and "Greatness" - find out what they are reffering to at Jefferson Davis's retirement home on a former plantation.

properties.name: Fort Massachusetts
properties.description: Run around in a mostly abandoned Civil War fort on an island that's part of Gulf Islands National Seashore. Only accessible by boat.

properties.name: Gateway Arch National Park
properties.description: The Gateway Arch is the world's tallest arch at 630ft tall. The National Park Service says you are explicitly allowed to touch it.

properties.name: City Museum
properties.description: The City museum is a 10 story giant adult playground maze with 10 story slides. To experience all the climbing and sliding make sure to bring quick dry athletic wear, knee pads, and zippered pockets or you will be full of regret.

properties.name: Erie Maritime Museum
properties.description: The USS Niagara played a pivotal war in winning the Battle of Lake Erie in the War of 1812, was sunk in 1820 raised in 1913, and rebuilt. The Niagara is the only warship that fought on the Great Lakes still afloat, and the second oldest American warship. The Erie Maritime Museum is located in a former power station and features history of the Battle of Lake Erie.

properties.name: Waldameer and Water World
properties.description: The only amusement park in the United States where you can bring your own beer and bring your own dog. Waldameer features Ravine Flyer II, a world renowned rollercoaster which crosses a highway by bridge twice. Waldameer is one of the best amusement parks I have ever been to, period.

properties.name: Drake Well Museum and Park
properties.description: Drake Well is the birthplace of the oil industry, all modern petroleum drilling and refining traces its roots back to the oil drilling boom started here in 1859.The world's first commerical oil well was so successful at producing oil that the price of oil dropped such that it became unprofitable.

properties.name: Kinzua Bridge State Park
properties.description: Climb over the corpse of a collapsed 301ft 1900 railroad bridge that was destroyed by a Tornado in 2003. The surviving span of bridge now acts as a walkway and observation point for the wreckage.

properties.name: Austin Dam Memorial Park
properties.description: In 1911 The Austin Dam failed and the resulting floodwaters killed 78 people. You can now hike and climb over the ruins of the site of the tradgedy which somehow wasn't the worst dam failure in Pennsylvania's history.

properties.name: Phil's Burrow
properties.description: Punxsutawney's entire economy is centered around the groundhog that lives at this burrow. Come see a town that is feverishly devoted to worshipping a marmot.

properties.name: Zippo Case Museum and Flagship Store
properties.street: Chestnut Street, 1932 Zippo Dr, Bradford, PA 16701
properties.description: Come see the destination devoted to starting tiny fires in your hand.

properties.name: National Comedy Center
properties.description: Jokes are funnier when you explain them with a museum.

properties.name: Letchworth State Park
properties.description: A 550ft gorge flanks 50 waterfalls, it's the Grand Canyon in green. The main waterfalls are over 100ft tall.

properties.name: JELL-O Museum
properties.street: 23 E Main St, Le Roy, NY 14482
properties.description: Learn about the history of America's most famous gelatin manufacturer in the town where it all started.

properties.name: Herschell Carrousel Factory Museum
properties.description: The source of most American carousels. North Tonawonda, NY used to be the home of 4 American Carrousel manufacturers, with Herschell lasting the longest. Herschell also invented the modern idea of amusement rides specially designed for small children. This museum operates several children's rides and has a functioning carousel that operates signifigantly faster than normal.

properties.name: Buffalo Naval Park
properties.street: 1 Naval, Marina Park S, Buffalo, NY 14202
properties.description: One of the most impressive naval collections in the United States. The only place where you can see a WW2 cruiser (Cleveland-class USS Little Rock), destroyer (Fletcher-class USS The Sulivans), submarine (Gato-class USS Croaker), and PT boat all in one place. The sail of the Los Angeles Class Submarine is also on display.

properties.name: Buffalo Transportation Pierce-Arrow Museum
properties.description: Pierce Arrow manufactured luxury cars akin to Rolls Royce from 1901 to 1938, and this museum contains just about every model they ever made as well as those of other defunct Western New York automakers. Additionally, the museum constructed a gas station designed by Frank Lloyd Wright because the plans looked really cool.

properties.name: Richardson Olmsted Campus
properties.description: Arkham asylum is based on this terrifying mental hospital - now a hotel!

properties.name: Niagara Falls State Park
properties.description: Niagara Falls State Park is located on an island separating the American Falls from Horseshoe Falls. Niagara falls is the highest flow rate of any waterfall in North America as the entirety of Lake Erie empties at this point into Lake Ontario at a rate of 5.9 million cubic feet per minute. The further you walk from the parking lot and the more stairs you take, the less crowded it gets - this is the American side after all.

properties.name: Niagara Power Vista Visitors Center
properties.description: Only 50% of the water in the Niagara River actually goes over Niagara Falls, the rest is diverted to a massive pair of dams paralleling each other in the 350ft Niagara Gorge.

properties.name: Whirlpool State Park
properties.street: 3100 Niagara Scenic Pkwy, Niagara Falls, NY 14305
properties.description: The Niagara River suddenly changes direction, causing turbulent water in the shape of a Whirlpool. The ever shifting whirlpool is most visible from the top of the gorge at Whirlpool State Park.

properties.name: Niagara Amusement Park and Splash World
properties.street: 2400 Grand Island Blvd, Grand Island, NY 14072
properties.description: Niagara Amusement Park and Splash world features charming cowboy shows, including a train robbery in this tranquil and slightly run-down amusement park. You can see the rising mist of Niagara Falls from the top of the Silver Comet rollercoaster, and get hammered in the waterpark.

properties.name: Medina Railroad Museum
properties.description: An old train station has been turned into a massive model train display.

properties.name: Seabreeze Amusement Park
properties.description: Seabreeze is a charming classic amusement park that has stuck to its history, featuring the Jack Rabbit - oldest rollercoaster in the United States, and the Bobsleds - the first modern hybrid steel-wooden rollercoaster. Seabreeze is situated on a hill overlooking Lake Ontario, and the view is stunning.

properties.name: The Strong National Museum of Play
properties.description: The Strong is home to the National Museum of Play, National Toy Hall of Fame, World Video Game oHall of Game, and the International Center for the History of Electronic Games. Your childhood? They have it.

properties.name: Stony Brook State Park
properties.description: Stone pathways let you get intimate with the curvaceous waterfalls and gorges of Stony Brook State Park. The state park has dammed a river such that it is now a natural swimming pool, complete with life guards.

properties.name: Bicycle Heaven
properties.description: This is THE bicycle museum. A hoard of 3000 bicycles kept in pristine conditions from all eras - and nearly all of them are for sale or for rent.

properties.name: Kamin Science Center
properties.description: The Kamin (formerly Carnegie) Science Center features the Robot Hall of Fame and the WW2 Tench-class submarine USS Requin. All those terrifying military robots that will surely be used against us? Their ancestors live here alongside the cute robots we see in movies and TV.

properties.name: Fort Necessity National Battlefield
properties.description: See where George Washington started the Seven Years War (or French and Indian War) by assassinating a French officer carrying a diplomatic message. This same war would lead to Britain imposing burdensome taxes on the American colonies to pay for their defense, leading directly to the American Revolutionary War where George Washington would be appointed the leading General for the revolutionaries.

properties.name: Fallingwater
properties.street: 1491 Mill Run Rd, Mill Run, PA 15464
properties.description: Wow, a super modern looking house built over a waterfall, bet that was built recently! Nope,  1936.  Frank Lloyd Wright's greatest architectural masterpiece.

properties.name: Kennywood
properties.description: Kennywood is home to three historical 1920s rollercoasters that take follow the terrain of the ravines cutting through the park. It is also home of Phantom's Revenge, one of the most acclaimed hypercoasters ever built. Kennywood is also home to the last surviving Turtle and Kangaroo ride.

properties.name: Lincoln Highway Experience
properties.description: Before the National Highway System, the Lincoln Highway nominally connected the East and West Coasts of the United States. In reality, it was a primitively paved dirt path. Learn the history of the Lincoln Highway and its tourist attractions. Your admission earns you a postcard , a cup of coffee, and a slice of pie inside of a historical diner.

properties.name: Idlewild and Soak Zone
properties.description: Idlewild (est. 1878) is a children's amusement park featuring Mr. Roger's Trolley (Now Daniel Tiger's Trolley, but I refuse to recognize that), and is the third oldest amusement park in the United States. Idlewild also features a land of children's storybooks come to life.

properties.name: Johnstown Flood National Memorial
properties.description: On May 31, 1889 the South Fork Fishing and Hunting Club's earten South Fork Dam collapsed during heavy rainfall, leading to a flood that destroyed the city of Johnstown and killed 2,208 people. The remains of the earthen dam is now available for tour.

properties.name: Heinz History Center
properties.description: The Heinz History Center features a prominent display by Heinz ketchup, Mr. Rogers set and puppets, and a replica of Elektro and Sparko (robots who are very dear to me).

properties.name: Brooklyn Bridge
properties.description: The Brooklyn Bridge opened as the longest suspension bridge in the world in 1883. The Brooklyn bridge was overengineered with more cables than needed, a stiffening truss system, granite towers, and generous factor of safety in design. This has allowed the bridge to smoothly transition from handling carriages to trains and automobiles with very little redesign. Walk across the bridge at least once to experience the New York City skyline from the middle of the river.

properties.name: 9/11 Memorial and Museum
properties.description: 2763 people were killed by the collapse of the World Trade Center on 9/11/2001. The site where the towers once stood is memorial fountains where waterfalls flow into the abyss giving the impression of a profound sense of emptiness and loss. The museum beneath the site captures the horror of the event and sells souvenirs and t-shirts.

properties.name: Empire State Building
properties.description: The Empire State Building opened in 1931 as the tallest building in the world at 1,454 ft, and held this record until the openeing of the World Trade Center in 1973. A masterpiece of Art Deco architecture the Empire State Building is an icon of New York City and the United States of America.

properties.name: Intrepid Museum
properties.street: Pier 86, W 46th St, New York, NY 10036
properties.description: The WW2 Essex-class aircraft carrier USS Intrepid has been turned into an aerospace museum, and because it's New York City they recieved the best aircraft political patronage could leverage. This includes the Space Shuttle Enterprise, a Concorde, Lockheed A-12, and the cold war era cruise missile submarine USS Growler.

properties.name: The Metropolitan Museum of Art
properties.description: The ultra-wealthy park their expensive paintings here for tax reasons. The Metropolitan Museum of Art possesses 2,000,000 works of art, including Washington Crossing the Delaware.

properties.name: Ellis Island National Museum of Immigration
properties.description: If you're from the United States, there's a good chance your ancestors got checked for diseases and poverty at Ellis Island Immigration Center along with the 12 million other immigrants who were processed here.

properties.name: Statue of Liberty
properties.description: Public donations funded what was then the tallest statue in the world in the heart of New York City. The torch is no longer accessible after German Empire saboteurs detonated an ammunition pier nearby in New Jersey in the Black Tom explosion. The Statue of Liberty remains an American icon worldwide - which is why you can buy a lego version of it.

properties.name: Rye Playland
properties.description: This 1927 Amusement Park set on the beach remains largely as it was opening day. Playland is one of the few municipally owned amusement parks in the United States.

properties.name: TWA Hotel
properties.description: The TWA Hotel is an example of 1950s futurism - basically it looks exactly like the movie The Incredibles.

properties.name: Bannerman Castle
properties.description: An abandoned military warehouse sits on an island in the middle of the Hudson River, where every view looks like a romance painting.

properties.name: Franklin D. Roosevelt Presidential Library and Museum
properties.street: 4079 Albany Post Rd, Hyde Park, NY 12538
properties.description: FDR combatted the Great Depression as governor of New York and took his programs nationwide, including: social security, insured bank accounts, federalized labor relations, agricultural price parity, mass deporations, and vast public works as executed through the Civilian Conservation Corps and Tennesee Valley Authority. FDR's policies were so popular the his party defied the typical midterm losses and increased its majorities. FDR leveraged this to win the presidency 4 times and died in office. Term limits exist solely because of him. The FDR Presidential Museum and Library is set on his family estate because he was a rich kid.

properties.name: USS Slater
properties.description: Sometimes you need a smaller than usual destroyer to escort other slow ships. The WW2 era Cannon-class USS Slater is one of the few remaining destroyer escorts afloat, and was once part of the Greek navy.

properties.name: Fort William Henry
properties.description: If you watched or read The last of The Mohicans, this is that fort. Fort William Henry was built in 1755 during the Seven Years War (French and Indian War). It was subjected to a siege in 1757 where the surrendering British were executed by the French's native allies.

properties.name: Fort Ticonderoga
properties.description: Fort Ticonderoga was built by the French in 1755 to control the scenic entrance to Lake Champlain. A large hill perfect for placing artillery overlooks Fort Ticonderoga, resultings in its capture by the British from the French in 1759, the Americans from the British in 1775, and the British from the Americans in 1777. Famously, the guns from the American capture in 1775 were hauled all the way to Boston to force the British to withdraw from the city during the American Revolution.

properties.name: Star Trek Original Series Set Tour
properties.description: Star Trek superfan James Cawley rebuilt the original Star Trek set from the original blueprints so that you too can gush over them.

properties.name: Adirondack Park
properties.description: 6.1 million acres of parkland in the mountainous backwoods of New York make Adirondack Park the biggest park in the Lower 48.

properties.name: Fort Stanwix National Monument
properties.description: This spikey looking fortress prevented the British from advancing down the Saratoga valley during the Revolutionary War, leading to their eventual defeat in the Saratoga Campaign, and the entrance of the French into the war on the side of the Americans. It's also just a really cool looking wooden fort.

properties.name: Buttermilk Falls State Park
properties.street: 106 E Buttermilk Falls Rd, Ithaca, NY 14850
properties.description: Pillars of rock, a narrow gorge, a swooshing water-carved creekbed, and a waterfall with a pathway that keeps you alongside it for all of its cascades makes Buttermilk Falls a must-see state park.

properties.name: Robert H. Treman State Park
properties.description: 12 waterfalls nestled in a steep gorge, including the 115ft Lucifer Falls. The cliffs are spectacular and the Gorge and Rim trails show you everything.

properties.name: Watkins Glen State Park
properties.street: 1009 N Franklin St, Watkins Glen, NY 14891
properties.description: Watkins Glen's stream descends 400ft past 200ft cliffs with 19 waterfalls along the way, the trail acompanies and winds over and under the waterfalls of the beautiful curved gorge, keeping you close to the action the whole time.

properties.name: Battleship Cove
properties.description: It's the world's largest collection of WW2 US Naval Ships, including the South Dakota class USS Massachusetts, the Gearing-class destroyer Jospey P Kennedy Jr., the Balao-class USS Lionfish, the Soviet Union built East German Tarantul-class corvette Hiddensee, and PT-796 and PT-617.

properties.name: Norman Rockwell Museum
properties.description: American artist Norman Rockwell painted extremely popular pictures that were seen by many Americans in the Saturday Evening Post. The Normal Rockwell Museum contains 574 of his works including the famous "Four Freedoms" paintings.

properties.name: American Heritage Museum
properties.description: By "American Heritage" they mean tanks, lots of operational tanks - that yes you can pay to ride in. These include the M1917A,  Matilda MK.II, Vickers Mk.IV, Churchill Crocodile, Cromwell I M4A1 Sherman, M3 Lee, M4A3E2 Sherman Jumbo, M22 Locust, M18 Hellcat , M5A1 Stuart VI, T-34, T34/85, Sturmgeschutz III, Panzer I.A, Panzer V, Jadgpanzer 38 Hetzer... you get the idea.

properties.name: Minute Man National Historical Park
properties.description: See where the American Revolutionary War began on April 19, 1775 when British forces tried to seize locals guns.

properties.name: Lowell National Historical Park
properties.description: Lowell Massachusetts was the center of the American textile industry, and its large textile mills still loom over the city (see what I did there). The textile mills that survive are available for tour.

properties.name: USS Constitution
properties.street: Building 22, Charlestown Navy Yard, Charlestown, MA 02129
properties.description: The USS Constitution was one of the original six frigates comissioned by Congress that marked the beginning of the United States Navy. The USS Constitution fought the French in the Quasi-War, the Babary Pirates in the First Barbary War, and the British in the War of 1812 and remains afloat to this day as the oldest ship in the United States Navy.

properties.name: USS Casin Young
properties.description: The WW2 era Fletcher-class destroyer USS Casin Young survived two kamikaze attacks and is still afloat today. Despite being a worthwhile attraction in its own right it is overshadowed by the fact that the USS Constitution is parked right to it.

properties.name: John F. Kennedy Presidential Library and Museum
properties.description: The one and only time the United States elected a young and attractive president he got his head blown off. This made the American public very sad, and since JFK was also a rich kid his Presidential Library is extremely opulent.

properties.name: United States Naval Shipbuilding Museum
properties.description: The WW2 era Des Moines-class cruiser USS Salem is back where it was built in Quincy. The Salem also offers ghost tours, and is also occasionally a haunted house.

properties.name: Plimoth Patuxet
properties.description: A living history museum portraying the initial Plymouth colony in Massachusetts. The museum gives a good idea of just how insane and precauious it was to move across the ocean to the middle of nowhere and be the first colonist, and how much of a cultist the Puritans had to be in order for it to be worth it.

properties.name: Springfield Armory National Historic Site
properties.description: Springfield Armory was the primary manufacturer for US military firearms from 1777 to 1968, when it was closed under the beliefs that it was more economical for private industry to produce firearms than the federal government. Springfield Armory National Historic Site contains all the firearms the United States government once produced for itself in the place they were produced.

properties.name: Museum of Fine Arts, Boston
properties.description: If I knew anything about art, I'm sure the 450,000 paintings at the Museum of Fine Arts in Boston would be really impressive to me.

properties.name: Gooseberry Falls State Park
properties.description: 4 waterfalls cascade over ancient lava flows into the world's largest freshwater lake at Gooseberry Falls State Park.

properties.name: Tettegouche State Park
properties.description: Rocky vertical cliffs on Lake Superior with a 70ft high waterfall.

properties.name: Judge CR Magney State Park
properties.description: Home of the Devil's Kettle, where the river splits into two waterfalls, one continuing the river's course, and the other plunging into a dark chasm with no visible reentry point.

properties.name: Grand Portage State Park
properties.description: A scenic 120ft waterfall marks the national border between the United States and Canada.

properties.name: Lake Vermillion-Soudan Underground Mine State Park
properties.description: Travel 2,341 feet to the depth of an iron mine in the Vermillion Range of Minnesota. The deepest and oldest iron mine in Minnesota (established 1882).

properties.name: SPAM Museum
properties.description: See how America's favorite processed meat made its way into our coronary arteries and our hearts.

properties.name: Mill City Museum
properties.description: Learn everything about industrial flour milling in the ruins of what was once the world's largest flour mill. Why ruins? It caught fire - flour mills do that.

properties.name: Hjemkomst Center
properties.description: Minnesotans celebrated their Scandanavian heritage by building a replica of the Hopperstad Stave Church and a replica of the Gokstand Viking longboat.

properties.name: Scandinavian Heritage Park
properties.description: Nothing quite says getting in touch with your ancestors like building a massive stave church and other Scandanavian buildings.

properties.name: Ronald Reagan Minuteman Missile State Historic Site
properties.description: The Dakotas are as far away from the ocean as one can get, which makes them an optimal place to put nuclear lauch facilities since any first strike much traverse the maximum distance possible to reach them. Descend into the Oscar-Zero Missile Alert Facility and November-33 Launch Facility to witness a nuclear missile launch facility with the power to end the world. You can't go into the actual missile silo, which is a shame.

properties.name: Theodore Roosevelt National Park
properties.description: 70,466 aces of badlands (with trees!) along the Little Missouri River. The park is divided into three units (South, North, Elkhorn Ranch) which all have their own unique flairs and scenic drives. It's a big National Park with around an hour of driving between each of the units.

properties.name: Little Missouri State Park
properties.description: It's like the badlands in nearby Teddy Roosevelt National Park, but much smaller.

properties.name: The Parthenon (Nashville)
properties.description: Nashville built an exact-size replica of the original Parthenon in Athens for the 1897 Tennessee Centennial Exposition -except this one wasn't destroyed by a gunpowder explosion.

properties.name: Lane Motor Museum
properties.description: The Lane Motor Museum is nearly entirely devoted to microcars and prototypes. See just how little of a car auto manufacturers tried to sell the public all over the world.

properties.name: Beech Bend
properties.street: 798 Beech Bend Park Rd, Bowling Green, KY 42101
properties.description: Beech Bend is a combined amusement-park-drag-strip with the imposing Kentucky Rumbler rollercoaster overlooking both. You haven't truly lived until you see racecars power down a drag strip while you plunge down the drop of a rollercoaster.

properties.name: National Corvette Museum
properties.description: A rare collection of corvettes from the nearby GM Bowling Green Assembly, including a few corvettes that fell down a sinkhole that opened in the middle of the museum.

properties.name: Mammoth Cave National Park
properties.street: Quarters 43, 1 Mammoth Cave Pkwy, Mammoth Cave, KY 42259
properties.description: Mammoth Cave is the world's largest cave system, it's so big in fact that it feels just like you're standing inside of a building, and it loses some of the magic. If you want to see any of the really cool stuff, you have to go on one of the guided tours which tend to be booked out weeks in advance - so plan ahead.

properties.name: Crystal Onyx Cave
properties.street: 425 Prewitts Knob Rd, Cave City, KY 42127
properties.description: Crystal Onyx cave differentiates itself from the other caves in the region by emphasizing how wacky it is. There is an esoteric collection of sculptures on the surface, and stunning formations below it.

properties.name: Creation Museum
properties.description: Australian Ken Ham Jesus Man and a team of ex-Universal Studios animatronics experts want to share their vision that the world is only around 6000 years old, and that mankind shared the planet with dinosaurs. Come and see expertly crafted intricate displays about the creation of the world according to their interpretation of the bible - including fully animatronic dinosaurs, a mockup Garden of Eden, and miniature Noah's Ark (the full sized one is down the road).

properties.name: Ark Encounter
properties.description: Australian Ken Ham Jesus Man and his team of Amish woodworkers built a life sized version of Noah's Ark from the bible and filled it with the animals that they thought would have been in it - dinosaurs. It is truly a sight to be hold, and seeing is believing.

properties.name: Fairway To Heaven Miniature Golf
properties.description: Golf your way through bible with 3 divine themed miniature golf courses: one for the Old Testament, one for the New Testament, and one for the miracles of Jesus.

properties.name: Cocaine Bear (bear)
properties.description: In 1985 a black bear overdosed on cocaine dropped by smugglers in the wilderness of Tennessee, and now sits stuffed at Kentucky for Kentucky where he can perform weddings if you believe he can. Cocaine Bear was eventually adapted into a feature film about the importance of family.

properties.name: Kentucky Derby Museum
properties.description: This is THE horse museum. Rich people who treat horses like F1 cars fly from all over the world  every year at Churchill Downs to watch the horses there run around a track once for two minutes. At the Kentucky Derby museums you can jump on a horse simulator and pretend that you too have importance to them.

properties.name: Louisville Mega Cavern
properties.description: An underground limestone mine is now a place where you can drive your car through caverns full of Christmas lights, aerial ropes courses, ziplines, and a historical tram tour.

properties.name: Harland Sanders Cafe and Museum
properties.description: Colonel Sanders started his fried chicken empire from this small cafe in Kentucky. This is THE Kentucky fried chicken he has been referring to this entire time.

properties.name: Natural Arch Kentucky
properties.description: A 100ft long sandstone natural arch in Daniel Boone National Forest that can be viewed from a commanding position on the bluffs, and easily hiked to be admired up close.

properties.name: Gorge Underground
properties.description: Kayak alone in a former limestone mine, you probably won't get lost.

properties.name: Hoover Dam
properties.street: 2785+G7, 81 Hoover Dam Access Rd, Boulder City, NV 89005
properties.description: See the only government infastructure project completed ahead of schedule. A 726ft Art Deco styled dam controlling the Colorado River in a 2000ft deep Canyon.

properties.name: Pinball Hall of Fame
properties.street: 4925 Las Vegas Blvd S, Las Vegas, NV 89119
properties.description: Get a better return than any Las Vegas casino because the money here goes straight to charity. 368+ pinball machines ranging from 1945-2024 eagerly await your quarters

properties.name: National Atomic Testing Museum
properties.street: 755 E Flamingo Rd, Las Vegas, NV 89119
properties.description: Nevada was the site of 928 nuclear bomb detonations during the USA's nuclear testing program, with the resulting mushroom clouds being visible to tourists in Las Vegas. The Atomic Museum covers the history of nuclear weapons development and testing, including nuclear rocket propoulsion, handheld nuclear weapons, nuclear bomb racks for underground testing, and nuclear weapons in culture.

properties.name: Machine Guns Vegas
properties.description: The Firearms Owners Protection Act of 1986 makes it illegal for civilians to own machine guns made after 1986. Fortunately, Machine Guns Vegas has a special license that exempts them from this law so that you can shoot things really fast without joining the military.

properties.name: Red Rock Canyon National Conservation Area
properties.description: In the washed out looking mountains of Nevada, the sharp red rocks of Red Rock canyon are visually striking.

properties.name: Valley of Fire State Park
properties.description: Swirly bright red and pastel pink petroglyph covered sandstone formations in the desert appear to be on fire when caught in the sun.

properties.name: Gold Butte National Monument
properties.description: Chiseled red sanstone, alien rock formations, and twisting canyons with petroglyphs. The roads aren't paved, and there's no real trails, so this is one of those 'not really near anything but wow nature' kind of parks.

properties.name: Tonopah Historic Mining Park
properties.description: You know you want to run around a 1900 delapitated desert silver mine. Look at the terrifyingly claustrophobic shafts propped up by logs doing their best.

properties.name: Nevada State Railroad Museum
properties.street: 2180 S Carson St, Carson City, NV 89701
properties.description: Pristine operational wild west railway trains in their native desert habitat. They also have a McKeen motor car that looks like a cross between a ship and a rail car. Yes you can ride the trains here.

properties.name: National Automobile Museum
properties.description: 220+ cars from casino magnate William Harrah's car collection are preserved here.

properties.name: Great Basin National Park
properties.street: National Park, 100 Great Basin, Baker, NV 89311
properties.description: Ancient pine trees, snowy mountain peaks, caves, and a rapidly retreating glacier set in the middle of the desert of the Great Basin.

properties.name: Lehman Caves
properties.description: twisted dripping and melting caves in the middle of Great Basin National Park. Reservations are sold out weeks in advance - so plan ahead.

properties.name: Cathedral Gorge State Park
properties.street: 111 Cathedral Gorge State Park Road, Panaca, NV 89042
properties.description: Erosion has carved the layered volcanic ash of a desert canyon into tall shear spires and caverns remniscent of a Cathedral.

properties.name: Space Needle
properties.description: A 605ft space age tower built for the 1962 World's Fair, and one of the only structures in the region built to withstand the inevitable 9.0 magnitude earthquake. This is the observation tower that all other observation towers try to imitate.

properties.name: Museum of Flight
properties.description: The largest private aircraft museum in the world featuring the planes of local aircraft manufacturer Boeing. The museum possesses 175 aircraft and spacecraft, including: the first presidential jet, a concorde, de Havilland Comet, Lockheed A-12, 727 prototype, 737, the first 747, 787, aerocar, and a DC-2.

properties.name: Flying Heritage and Combat Armor Museum
properties.description: They sliced a tank in half here so you can get a good look at it.

properties.name: Future of Flight Aviation Center and Boeing Tour
properties.description: This is where planes are born. Tour the largest building in the world at the Boeing Everett Production Facitiliy and see Boeing planes roll down the assembly line.

properties.name: America's Car Museum
properties.description: Harold LeMay amassed the largest private car collection in the world.The 350 cars at America's Car Museum are only half the the LeMay car collection, the other half is available at the LeMay Family Collection at Marymount.

properties.name: LeMay Collections at Marymount
properties.description: Whereas America's Car Museum is an ordered sample of Harold LeMay's car collection, the LeMay Collections at Marymount is a chaotic warehouse of 500+ classic cars.

properties.name: United States Naval Undersea Museum
properties.description: The nearby city of Bremerton is home of the Pacific Nuclear Submarine Fleet, and this is their museum. Featuring the control room from the USS Greenling, the Bathyscaphe Trieste II which was used to recover fallen satellite packages, and the Deep Submergence Rescue Vehicle

properties.name: USS Turner Joy
properties.description: The Cold War era Forrest Sherman-class destroyer USS Turner Joy is the only naval ship that the public can go on near Naval Station Bremerton. The USS Turner Joy was present during the Gulf of Tonkin Incident that was the catalyst for the U.S. involvement in the Vietnam War.

properties.name: Snoqualmie Falls
properties.description: A hotel is perched on the edge of a cliff overlooking a 270ft scenic waterfall.

properties.name: W.T. Preston
properties.description: The W.T. Preston is a United States Army Corps of Engineers sternwheeler snagboat that removed logjams and navigational hazards on rivers in the Puget sound from 1931-1981.

properties.name: North Cascades National Park
properties.description: 300 glaciers crowning the jagged peaks and shear cliffs of the North Cascades Range. It's the most expansive glacial system in the lower 48. Explore crystal clear lakes, waterfalls, and river valleys by trail or wilderness hiking as there's fairly little infrastructure here.

properties.name: Olympic National Park
properties.street: 3002 Mt Angeles Rd, Port Angeles, WA 98362
properties.description: Olympic National Park is a sea-stack strewn beach with a coastal rainforest next to a mountain range covered in glaciers and waterfalls. Olympic National Park is also the exlusive home of the Olympic Marmot, the Washington State Mammal.

properties.name: Mount Ranier National Park
properties.description: A 14,410ft active stratovolcano towers over 25 glaciers, plummeting waterfalls, racing streams,  rocky gorges, hotsprings, and a rainforest. The volcano divides the parks into four distinct regions with their own visitors centers: Paradise, Longmire, Sunrise, Ohanapecosh, and Carbon River.

properties.name: Mount St. Helens National Volcanic Monument
properties.street: 3029 Spirit Lake Hwy, Castle Rock, WA 98611
