properties.description: A smoldering 8363ft stratovolano towers over an ashen river valley and lava tube caves. The Johnston Ridge Observatory contains a museum regarding the 1980 eruption

properties.name: Hanford B
properties.description: Hanford B was the first large-scale nuclear reactor ever built, it provided plutonium for the construction of the nuclear weapons as part of the Manhattan Project in 1944. The abandoned reactor is now part of the Manhattan Project National historical Park, tours are available and are the only way for tourists to get onto the secured site. Call ahead.

properties.name: Maryhill Stonehenge
properties.description: A 1929 replica of Stonehenge overlooks the Columbia river in Maryhill Washington.

properties.name: Spokane Falls
properties.description: Spokane Falls rushes through the the futuristic Riverfront Park in downtown Spokane.

properties.name: Palouse Falls State Park Heritage Site
properties.description: The 200ft Palouse Falls is situated in a bowl-shaped canyon with tiered cliffs, and is the official state waterfall of Washington.

properties.name: Sun Lakes-Dry Falls State Park
properties.street: 34875 Park Lake Rd NE, Coulee City, WA 99115
properties.description: During the ancient Missoula Floods, a 400ft tall and 3.5 mile wide waterfall stripped the landscape here down to the volcanic basalt. The devastation from the floods tore the landscape into a barren canyon.

properties.name: Lake Chelan National Recreation Area
properties.description: A pictureseque lake next to the North Cascades range is only accessible by passenger ferry, floatplane, or hiking.

properties.name: Evergreen Aviation and Space Museum
properties.description: Home of the largest intact aircraft: The 1947 Hughes H-4 Hercules Spruce Goose. Notable aircraft also include a de Havilland Venom, SR-71 Blackbird, F-117 Nighthawk, X-15, and X38 Also a part of the museum is the Wings and Waves waterpark, where you can take 4 waterslides out of a retired Boeing 747.

properties.name: Crater Lake National Park
properties.street: Crater Lake National Park, Rim Village, CRATER LAKE, OR 97604
properties.description: A 1949ft deep lake inside of the remnants of a 6 mile wide destroyed volcano. Other extinct volcanos surround the park, as do pinnacled badlands and old growth forests.

properties.name: Toketee Falls
properties.description: A 120ft waterfall pours through an opening in columnar basalt cliffs in the thick woods of Umpqua National Forest near the entrance to Crater Lake National Park.

properties.name: Fort Stevens State Park
properties.description: An overgrown WW2 fort overlooks the beaches of the ever shifting mouth of the Colombia River and the shipwreck of the Peter Iredale.

properties.name: Bonneville Salt Flats
properties.street: Bonneville Salt Flats State Park, Wendover, UT 84083
properties.description: The flat lifeless salt plains here are the dried up remains of a 100 mile long ancient lake. This flatness has been put to optimal use by the Bureau of Land Management - as a high speed drag strip to set land speed records.

properties.name: Golden Spike National Historical Park
properties.description: In 1869 the United States completed the longest railroad ever built and united the tracks of the nation with a single Golden Spike. Working replicas of the locomotives that met are present and reenactments of the Golden Spike ceremony are held here on a seasonal schedule.

properties.name: Great Sand Dunes National Park and Preserve
properties.description: The tallest sand dunes in the United States are between the Rocky Mountains and some grassland. Sand from dried up ancient lakes has piled dunes against the snowcapped mountains. These are the tallest sand dunes in North America with some up to 750ft tall.

properties.name: Capulin Volcano National Monument
properties.description: Hike the rim and crater of a 1000ft extinct cone volcano surrounded by lush grassland. Don't worry, you can drive your car to the top - this is America after all.

properties.name: Little Jerusalem Badlands State Park
properties.street: County Road 400 and Gold Road, Oakley, KS 67748
properties.description: Are the soaring badlands of Badlands National Park too tall for you? Are there too many people? What if I told you there were 100ft tall miniature badlands that you can easily hike up and down and all around. Stay on the trails, the Niobrara Chalk formations are soft and easily damaged, and this is all western Kansas really has going for it.

properties.name: Tallgrass Prarie National Preserve
properties.description: Grassland so flat and grassy that the Federal government decided to preserve it as the definition of grassland.

properties.name: Big Brutus
properties.description: The second largest electric shovel ever built was designed to strip the Kansas coal fields from 1962 to 1974. This 160ft piece of machinery is the museum - quite literally, the interior has been transformed into a museum space.

properties.name: J. M. Davis Arms and Historical Museum
properties.street: 330 N J M Davis Blvd, Claremore, OK 74017
properties.description: This is THE gun museum in the United States. 12,000 firearms are stored in seemingly endless rows of shelves. All because J.M. Davis's dad bribed his child to take his medicine with the promise of a shotgun - beginning a lifelong obsession.

properties.name: Strataca
properties.description: When you think "Kansas" do you think 150 miles of endless labyrinthian underground tunnels from which you may never escape? Travel in electric tram through 40ft tall salt mining tunnels 650ft below the surface to see the world's greatest salt mining museum. The massive salt mine also sees use as a 26 acre underground vault and storage area for valuable documents and film.

properties.name: Cosmosphere
properties.description: Going upwards is really fascinating to people that live in a land as flat as a pancake. The Cosmosphere is the largest collection of Soviet space artifacts outside of Moscow. Home to the Apollo 13 command module, Soviet Union Vostock and Voskhod 2 space capsules, a Titan II rocket; the actual filght-ready backup models for Sputnik 1, Sputnik 2, and Vanguard; replicas of the Space Shuttle Endeavour, and much much more.

properties.name: Dwight D. Eisenhower Presidential Library, Museum and Boyhood Home
properties.description: Eisenhower was just a dude from Kansas who joined the military in 1915 and rose through the ranks. Being Supreme Allied Commander while winning the biggest war in history made him popular enough to win the presidency. Eisenhower enforced Civil Rights legislation, built the USA's highway system, started NASA and presided over the most prosperous economic period in American history. America has never again elected a man without a full head of hair.

properties.name: Oz Museum
properties.street: 511 Road to Oz Highway, Wamego, KS 66547
properties.description: Kansas is best known internationally for being the place Dorothy from the Wizard of Oz chose over staying in a magical world. At the Oz museum you can watch her repeat this decision over and over again in their theater. You can also take pictures with various recreations of the set and characters.

properties.name: London Museum Cafe and Soda Fountain
properties.description: On May 18. 1937 a natural gas leak destroyed the London School in New London Texas, killing 311 teachers and students while their parents watched helplessly from the PTA meeting held in the adjacent gym. That's why mercaptan is added to gas to make it smell bad. Honor the memory of the third-worst disaster in Texas by eating ice cream at this soda fountain and local history museum.

properties.name: Texas Broadcast Museum
properties.description: This is THE broadcasting museum. It's everything television broadcasting at the Texas Broadcasting Museum. Come see the DuMont Telecruiser, the ESPN mobile unit, a fully functioning TV studio, radio studio, piles of television cameras, broadcasting equipment, and endless radios.

properties.name: Crater of Diamonds State Park
properties.description: Go out in a 37-acre field and dig for real diamonds - and yes, you can keep them.

properties.name: Arnolds Park Amusement Park
properties.description: A  Roaring Twenties amusment park on the Iowa Great Lakes is lost in time and maintains its classic charm. Come ride their 100 year old rollercoaster and a rollercoaster that has no seat belt.

properties.name: Hot Springs National Park
properties.description: These unique 143F hot springs aren't volcanic, but instead are a result of groundwater circulation through folded rock. A spa town formed around these hot springs as a result.  Eight historical bathhouses are part of 'Bathhouse Row" and are available for tour at this combined geothermal-architectural National Park.

properties.name: Arkansas Inland Maritime Museum
properties.street: 120 Riverfront Park Dr, North Little Rock, AR 72114
properties.description: The tugboat Hoga survived the attack on Pearl Harbor in 1941 and is one of the last surviving ships from that day. The WW2 era Balao-class submarine and nuclear testing survivor USS Razorback is also sitting here in the Arkansas River, 350miles away from the nearest ocean.

properties.name: William J. Clinton Presidential Library and Museum
properties.street: 1200 President Clinton Ave, Little Rock, AR 72201
properties.description: President Bill Clinton really chose to make his museum shaped like a single long elevated shaft.

properties.name: Titanic Museum (Branson, Missouri)
properties.description: In only 100 short years a national tragedy can become a fun museum. See interior re-creations of the RMS Titanic, hop in a lifeboat or slide down the slanted deck. All that and more at this 1/3 scale replica of the front half of the RMS Titanic.

properties.name: Silver Dollar City
properties.street: 399 Silver Dollar City Pkwy, Branson, MO 65616
properties.description: An amusement park where it's always the 1880s, and that includes a spectacular caving experience built right into the park. Silver Dollar City consistently ranks as one of the top amusement parks in the world. Silver Dollar City's rollercoaster Outlaw Run ranks consistently in the top 10 wooden rollercoasters on the planet.

properties.name: Christ of the Ozarks
properties.street: 937 Passion Play Rd, Eureka Springs, AR 72632
properties.description: Come see the 67ft "Milk Carton Jesus", a replica of the Holy Land, and the Berlin Wall; all on top of a mountain in the Ozarks.

properties.name: Buffalo National River
properties.description: 135 mile of bluffs, canyons, waterfalls, and panoramic views - it's the perfect place to Kayak. A lot of the better looking hikes are in the Upper District. With 135 miles of river, you need to know where you are going - so plan ahead.

properties.name: Pinnacle Mountain State Park
properties.description: A rocky tetrahedron-shaped mountain offers stunning views of the islands in the Arkansas River and nearby lakes.

properties.name: Petit Jean State Park
properties.street: 1285 Petit Jean Mountain Rd, Morrilton, AR 72110
properties.description: A 95ft waterfall, impressive canyons, caves, arches, and a rocky mountaintop overlooking the Arkansas River explain why Petit Jean was made the first Arkansas State Park.

properties.name: Mount Magazine State Park
properties.description: Mount Magazine is the highest point in Arkansas(2753ft) and offers commanding views from its bluffs and lodge. There's a road to the top because this is America.

properties.name: United States Marshals Museum
properties.description: The United States Marshals Service is the original U.S. federal law enforcement agency from the founding of the nation. Learn about their history in this highly stylized museum that focuses how U.S. Marshals acted as source of the law in the frontier.

properties.name: The Walmart Museum
properties.description: International retail giant Walmart got its start at this humble store in this small Arkansas town. Fortunately, Walmart has followed its founder Sam Walton's vision of treating employees well, quality American-made products, and low prices.

properties.name: Top of The Rock, Branson, Missouri
properties.street: 150 Top of the Rock Rd, Ridgedale, MO 65739
properties.description: You can drive a golf cart through a waterfall filled cave here. Privately owned lake-view vistas, waterfalls, caves with waterfalls, and pinnacles tour all conducted by golf cart at the top of a cliff near Branson Missouri. Make sure to check out the Lost Canyon Cave and Nature Trail and Ancient Ozarks Natural History Museum.

properties.name: Dogwood Canyon and Nature Park
properties.description: The official park of Bass Pro Shops founder Johny Morris. Layered plate-like cliffs and waterfalls dot this canyon at this 10,000-acre privately owned park near Branson, Missouri.

properties.name: Wonders of Wildlife Museum and Aquarium
properties.description: This is the first Bass Pro Shops, and it features the massive Wonders of Wildlife Aquarium, the IGFA Fishing Hall of Fame, and the NRA National Sporting Arms Museum. Yes they have Japanese Spider Crabs.

properties.name: Blanchard Springs Caverns
properties.description: See 1.2 miles of springfed caverns descending 366ft below the surface of of a hilltop. The caverns end by rocketing out of a waterfall pushing its way out of a hole in the cliff. Blanchard Springs Caverns are part of the Ozark-St. Francis National Forests.

properties.name: Cosmic Cavern
properties.description: Trout-filled caverns with notable soda-straw like formations and bottomless underground lakes. Seriously - they haven't found the bottom of the lakes yet.

properties.name: Fantastic Caverns
properties.description: These caverns are so massive you can drive a car through them, and you do. Take an hour long jeep-towed journey through the path of an ancient underground river.

properties.name: Ha Ha Tonka State Park
properties.description: Explore an abandoned mansion on the edge of the soaring cliffs of Ha Ha Tonka State Park. The surroundings are gorgeous too with sinkholes, waterfalls, caves, and a natural bridge.

properties.name: Harry S. Truman Presidential Library and Museum
properties.description: Harry S. Truman replaced Henry A. Wallace as Vice President because Wallace was considerd too left-wing, and as a result became President upon President Franklin Delano Roosevelt's Death. Truman authorized the first use of nuclear weapons in war, the Berlin Airlift, desegregation of the armed forces, and began demilitarization following the victory of WW2. As a result the nation found itself unprepared for the Korean War.

properties.name: National World War I Museum and Memorial
properties.description: Kansas residents started a fundraising drive in 1919 and as a result the WWI memorial was built in Kansas City in 1926. The memorial features a massive stone observation tower, and a museum to the second largest war fought so far in the European thunderdome.

properties.name: Forest Park (St. Louis)
properties.description: Forest Park is the former site of the 1904 World's Fair - and with the number of free world class museums its as if the World's Fair is still happening. Forest Park features: the St Louis Zoo, St. Louis Art Museum, Missouri History Museum, art deco greenhouse, and the St. Louis Science Center.

properties.name: Bonne Terre Mine
properties.description: Go scuba diving around abandoned mining equipment at the world's largest subterranean lake in a submerged 150-year old lead mine. There's also a brief boat tour if swimming in a lead mine sounds like a bad idea to you. It gets busy - so plan ahead.

properties.name: Meramec State Park
properties.description: Most spectacular cave tours have lighting - this one doesn't. So keep your hands on your flashlight, and don't stray off the path.

properties.name: Onondaga Cave State park
properties.description: Onondaga cave is tall, REALLY tall and there's a mile of it for tours. If Onondaga cave isn't enough for you there is also Cathedral Cave which looks as if the ceiling is melting.

properties.name: Enchanted Forest (Oregon)
properties.description: Enchanted Forest amusement park converted a waterslide into a in-house built rollercoaster, the resulting engineering creation is a beautiful monstrosity. Additionally the park has a re-creation of various fairy tales, and they look right in place in the haunted forests of Oregon.

properties.name: Iowa 80
properties.description: Go Truck Yourself at the world's largest truck stop! Go to the truck museum, the truck movie theater, the truck dentist, the truck church, the truck gift shop, and the SUPER TRUCK SHOWROOM. It's a trucker's paradise - except that it's in Iowa.

properties.name: Herbert Hoover Presidential Museum and Library
properties.description: Herbert Hoover was born on a ranch, became a wealthy mining engineer, saved Belgium from starvation in World War I as the head of the Belgian relief Commission, saved Russia and Eastern Europe from starvation as head of the American Relief Administration, presided over the economic boom of the Roaring Twenties as Commerce Secretary, and successfully led the active Federal response to the Great Mississippi Flood of 1927. Herbert Hoover's work undoubtably saved millions of lives by the time he took office in 1929 - surely he would go down in history as a good president.

properties.name: John Deere Tractor And Engine Museum
properties.description: Behold the evolution of the tractor and the cult of John Deere.

properties.name: Maquoketa Caves State Park
properties.description: Natural bridges, 13 caves, rock strewn hills, and soaring bluffs - all somehow in Iowa. I'm probably underselling it, but a speed camera ticketed me in Iowa and that's impacting my favor.

properties.name: The National Mississippi River Museum And Aquarium
properties.description: If the boatshop and the 1934 river dredge William M. Black don't convince you to come here, the National Mississippi River Museum and Aquarium also has a Giant Pacific Octopus and river otters.

properties.name: George M. Verity (towboat)
properties.description: See a  Mississippi River 1927 paddlewheeler towboat, one of the few Mississippi museum paddlewheelers that actually carried cargo and looks like how you imagine a paddlewheel ship would look.

properties.name: Devils Tower
properties.street: Devils Tower-National Monument Rd, Devils Tower, WY 82714
properties.description: The core of a dead volcano petrified on the surface of Wyoming. Native American tribes rumor that this near vertical 1,267ft columnar butte was formed by massive bears scraping their claws against its sides.

properties.name: Independence Rock
properties.description: An out of place bulbous 130ft rock between two mountain ranges is inscribed with the names of the settlers who passed by it on the Oregon Trail. If you ever played Oregon Trail, you know this rock well.

properties.name: Yellowstone National Park
properties.description: One day the Yellowstone Caldera will erupt and scour half of North America. For now, enjoy 2.2 million acres of geysers, bubbling hot springs, 350+ waterfalls,  and dazzling canyons of the world's first National Park.

properties.name: Old Faithful Inn
properties.street: 3200 Old Faithful Inn Rd, Yellowstone National Park, WY 82190
properties.description: The largest log structure in the world is built next to the Old Faithful Geyser. It's all wood and is a masterpiece within its own right. This is the massive lodge that all park lodges try to imitate.

properties.name: Bannack State Park
properties.description: A real mining ghost town in the dry hills of Montana. Yes you can go in the buildings - it's encouraged.

properties.name: Castles N Coasters
properties.street: 9445 N Metro Pkwy E, Phoenix, AZ 85051
properties.description: Home of the official Operation Desert Storm rollecoaster. The arcade feels like what it must have been like to enter Saddam Hussein's palace. Stray cats roam the immaculate landscaping of the mini golf courses and live in the tiny structures there.

properties.name: Saguaro National Park
properties.street: 3693 S Old Spanish Trail, Tucson, AZ 85730
properties.description: These cacti are nothing like the little plants you leave to die in your windowsill - they're 60ft tall and live for 100 years. There is a whole forest of Saguaro Cacti in Saguaro National Park. The park is divided into two districts: the Tucson Mountain District and the Rincon Mountain District, each with their own visitor's center and trails.

properties.name: Pima Air And Space Museum
properties.description: This is THE air and space museum. Look, I know I said that about the USAF museum, but this is a close second. 400+ aircraft lay over 80-acres and 6 hangers akin to an aircraft boneyard in the Arizona desert. You can walk up to most of the aircraft, there are no ropes or fences, but the hot metal is its own deterrent. Featuring 3 different B-52s, A B-36 (the largest bomber ever built), YC-14, SR-71, B-58, an airborne observatory inside of a 747, etc....basically every aircraft you could ever want to see.

properties.name: Biosphere 2
properties.description: The largest closed ecological system ever constructed designed to simulate a life support system for space colonization. Every biome is simulated: rainforest, ocean (complete with coral reef), mangrove wetlands, savnnah grassland, and a fog desert. Now available for tour - and this time the humans inside won't run out of oxygen.

properties.name: Titan Missile Museum
properties.street: 1580 W Duval Mine Rd, Green Valley, AZ 85614
properties.description: Nuclear missile silo complete with nuclear missile. Titan II missiles were the backbone of the USAs land based deterrent until the Minuteman missile series. You can go into the control room and look at the missile on various tours.

properties.name: Chiricahua National Monument
properties.street: 12856 East Rhyolite Creek Road, Willcox, AZ 85643
properties.description: It really looks like someone had just spent the past few thousand years balancing rocks on top of each other. Hoodoos, arches, and balancing rocks as far as the eyes can see. All formed from eroded volcanic ash.

properties.name: Grand Canyon National Park
properties.street: 8 S Entrance Rd, Grand Canyon Village, AZ 86023
properties.description: This is THE Canyon. 277 miles of mile deep canyon, and you start at the top looking down. Even if there is snow at the top, the bottom is still a scorching desert. If you plan to hike it, it is way harder to go down than it is to go back up, and NO you can't drive to the bottom despite this being America.

properties.name: Havasu Creek
properties.description: Havasu Creek is a bright blue stream on the Havasupai indian Reservation home to meandering waterfall oasis canyons in the hot desert. This includes the 100ft Havasu Falls. Good luck getting there - the only way in is by helicopter, hiking, or riding a donkey.

properties.name: Vermillion Cliffs National Monument
properties.description: The arches and canyons here look like the layered brush strokes of a Van-gough painting. You need a permit. There's no roads - so once you're in you can roam free. Make sure to check out The Wave at the Coyote Buttes North trailhead - which is only accessible by daily lottery.

properties.name: Antelope Canyon
properties.description: The curved canyons of Antelope Canyon look straight out of the movie Dune and is exclusively accessible through guided tours.

properties.name: Navajo National Monument
properties.description: Massive alcoves in the cliffs are full of the ancient Native American cliff-dwelling villages.

properties.name: Monument Valley
properties.description: Massive sandstone buttes stand alone in the desert. These are the quintessential images of the American Southwest.

properties.name: Canyon de Chelly National Monument
properties.description: A 750ft vertical sandstone spire, ancient cliff dwellings, and sheer cliffs. Visits to the canyon floor are only by permit or tour.

properties.name: Petrified Forest National Park
properties.street: 1 Park Rd, Petrified Forest National Park, AZ 86028
properties.description: Ancient forests have toppled over and turned to rainbow colored stone in this colorful canyon.

properties.name: Meteor Crater
properties.description: The most obvious sign of a meteor impact you are ever gong to see on this planet a - 3700ft wide crater. The actual meteor is in the visitor's center here.

properties.name: Slide Rock State Park
properties.description: Slide Rock State Park is like if the Grand Canyon had lots and lots of very green trees while still being made of tall red rock.

properties.name: Coconino National Forest
properties.description: Pretty much all of the forests and canyons of Arizona are part of Cococino National Forest - this includes all the beautiful trails out in Sedona. There are simply too many beautiful sites within the forest to choose from, so the entire forest has been included.

properties.name: Hall of Flame Fire Museum
properties.street: 6101 E Van Buren St, Phoenix, AZ 85008
properties.description: This is THE firetruck/firefighting museum. The world's largest firefighting museum has over 130 firetrucks. Arizona is a desert, so things catch on fire a lot here.

properties.name: Organ Pipe Cactus National Monument
properties.description: Organ Pipe Cactus are a bundle of stems that grow up to 26ft in height, and at Organ Pipe Cactus National Monument there's a whole forest of them.

properties.name: Arizona-Sonora Desert Museum
properties.description: All the cool wildlife and plants of Arizona in one beautifully landscaped place. Coyotes, prarrie dogs, bighorn sheep, cougars, hawks, and owls.

properties.name: Tombstone, Arizona
properties.description: The entire city of Tombstone, Arizona has preserved its boomtown architecture and heritage of wild-west gunfights. The gunfight at the O.K. Corral happened here, and formed the archetype of the American Wild West.

properties.name: Kartchner Caverns State Park
properties.description: 2.4 miles of stunning 50,000 year old limestone caves in the Arizona desert. Get a reservation, this cave is busy.

properties.name: Old Tucson Studios
properties.description: This is literally the wild west town you see in movies and television.  That's because pretty much every production that needed a wild west setting was filmed here at this movie studio from 1939-present.

properties.name: Falls Park
properties.street: 131 E Falls Park Dr, Sioux Falls, SD 57104
properties.description: Rushing waters over pink rock with no guardrails to stop you. Seriously, you can hop on the rocks until you are in the middle of the waterfall.

properties.name: Palisades State Park
properties.description: Pink rock forms 50ft tall vertical cliffs and freestanding stacks and hoodoos at Palisades State Park.

properties.name: Devils Gulch Park
properties.description: Outlaw Jesse James jumped the  raging rapids and pink quartize pinnacles of this chasm on horseback. Now you can walk it thanks to the handy steel grate bridge.

properties.name: Minuteman Missile National Historic Site
properties.description: There are 450 active Minuteman III  nuclear missiles in the surrounding area, visit their retired sibling the Minuteman II and its launch control system. Tour the Delta-01 Launch Control Facility to see the keys to armageddon, then pop on by the Delta-09 Minuteman Missile Silo. You will need to book a tour - it's a nuclear missile silo.

properties.name: Badlands National Park
properties.description: 244,000 acres of the most scenic badlands in the world. Bighorn sheep and prarrie dogs are abundant, and the vistas are seemingly endless. Because it's America, you can tour the entire rim by automobile.

properties.name: Mount Rushmore National Memorial
properties.description: The USA carved massive 60ft scultpures of its best presidents into the Black Hills of South Dakota. It's very far away from the viewing platform, so it looks much smaller in person. This is the sculpture that all other sculptures carved into mountainsides tries to imitate.

properties.name: Black Elk Peak
properties.description: The highest point in South Dakota with a perfect view to take in all the beauty of the Black Hills. There's an observation tower at the very top. The best trailhead is located in Custer State Park.

properties.name: Custer State Park
properties.description: If Custer State Park wasn't a state park, it would be a national park - that's how good it is. All the trails that are worth going to: Black Elk Peak, Cathedral Spires, Needles Eye Tunnel, Sunday Gulch, etc. are all here. The Wildlife Loop Road lets you get literally next to wild Bison who are acclimated to cars.

properties.name: Black Hills National Forest
properties.description: The Black Hills are a mountainous island of green  surrounded by the Great Plains. Black Hills National Forest contains most of the trails and scenic roadways, with the rest being part of Custer State Park.

properties.name: Spearfish Canyon
properties.description: Spearfish canyon is a gorge filled with waterfalls part of the Black Hills National Forest. Make sure to check out Spearfish Falls and Roughlock falls.

properties.name: Homestake Mine (South Dakota)
properties.description: This 8000ft deep former gold mine has been converted into into the Deep Underground Science and Engineering Laboratory - the deepest underground laboratory in the United States. Research into dark matter and neutrinos is conducted there due to the ability to escape cosmic radiation. Now you can stare into the void of the pit of the mine - which is a sight in itself.

properties.name: Crazy Horse Memorial
properties.description: This mountainside carving will be the largest in the world if it's ever completed - the face alone is larger than the heads of Mount Rushmore.

properties.name: Wind Cave National Park
properties.description: The boxwork walls of Wind Cave look like a terrifying spiderweb, and the cave breathes as if you were in the innards of some horrible creature. You have to purchase a tour to see the caves, and you can only do that at the visitor's center the day of.

properties.name: Jewel Cave National Monument
properties.description: Calcite crystals line the walls of this 220 mile breathing cave in the Black Hills of South Dakota. You need a reservation to visit this busy cave, so try to book months in advance online.

properties.name: The Caverns
properties.description: Have you ever wanted to listen to a rave inside of a cave. Now you can at The Caverns - the only concert venue I know of inside of a cave.  There's also cave tours, but those are just OK.

properties.name: Big South Fork National River and Recreation Area
properties.description: Explore towering cliffs, natural bridges, waterfalls, and the abandoned mining town of Blue Heron, Kentucky - all nestled close to the Big South Fork Cumberland River.

properties.name: Titanic Museum (Pigeon forge, Tennessee)
properties.description: It only takes 100 years for a tragedy to become a romance. See the half-scale replica of the front half of the Titanic at the world's largest permanent Titanic museum. If you are rooting for the iceberg - I've got good news for you.

properties.name: Dollywood
properties.street: 2700 Dollywood Parks Blvd, Pigeon Forge, TN 37863
properties.description: The official amusement park of country music star and future saint: Dolly Parton, and consistently ranked among the top amusement parks worldwide.

properties.name: Great Smoky Mountains National Park
properties.street: 1420 Fighting Creek Gap Rd, Gatlinburg, TN 37738
properties.description: It's a temperate rainforest right here in the Appalachians. Waterfalls, cliffs, and endless rocky mountains covered in mist that resembles smoke. Make sure to check out Kuwohi (Clingman's Dome) - the highest point in the park.

properties.name: Craighead Caverns
properties.description: Sail through caverns at the United State's largest underground lake - yes there's a waterfall and trout down here.

properties.name: Chickamauga and Chattanooga National Military Park
properties.street: 110 Point Park Rd, Lookout Mountain, TN 37350
properties.description: 20,000 soldiers fought through the clouds on top of Lookout Mountain for control of Chatanooga, as a part of the broader Chatnooga campaign of the U.S. Civil War.  Chickamauga was the largest battle of the Western Theater where 34,000 soldiers became casualties. Now you can walk the battlefields with a sky-high view of the city in the river-valley below.

properties.name: Ruby Falls
properties.description: A 60ft waterfall inside of a cave on top of Lookout Mountain - only accessible by tour.

properties.name: Fall Creek Falls State Park
properties.description: A 256ft tall waterfall surrounded by bowl shaped cliffs is the main star of this park - but there's 7 other waterfalls and 4 caves if that's not enough for you. The waterfall and gorge have scenic overlooks and unsafe feeling rope bridges if somehow all other other things weren't enough for you. It's the most visited state park in Tennesse for a reason.

properties.name: Cumberland Caverns
properties.description: This cave is so large that they host concerns inside of it.  There's five seperate walking tours which do not even begin to cover the 32 miles of mapped passages.

properties.name: Rock Island State Park (Tennessee)
properties.description: Twin Falls bursts seemingly out of nowhere from a cavern in the lush cliffs into the Caney Fork River just downstream of the Great Falls Dam. The cliffs, rapids, and gorge here are also quite impressive with a series of smaller waterfalls. There is also a derelict cotton mill in the woods available to explore.

properties.name: Burgess Falls State Park
properties.description: A 136ft waterfall anchors this series of 4 waterfalls through a gorge in the forests of Tennessee. If it doesn't look tall enough, you can swim and kayak at the base and look up at the towering wall of rock and water above you (though you have to paddle 4 miles upriver to do so).

properties.name: Cummins Falls State Park
properties.description: The base of this 75ft waterfall and gorge are accessible with a permit to splash about in the tiers of cascades and rocks.

properties.name: Knoebels Amusement Resort
properties.description: Knoebels is a coal-mining themed amusement park/resort/lumber yard. Ride the coal-mining themed rollercoaster, tour the coal-mining museum, and buy little coal mining helmets for your kids. Knoebels is also home to the renowned rollercoaster Phoenix, considered the best wooden rollercoaster ever built - it has won the Golden Ticket Awards Top Wooden Rollercoaster from 2018-2025. Knoebels also operates the only wooden bobsled coaster in the world: Flying Turns.

properties.name: Ricketts Glen State Park
properties.description: 24 waterfalls with stone plate pathways precariously flanking their sides. The trees form a perfect canopy meaning you are fully enclosed by the ridges, streams, and forests of Ricketts Glen State Park.

properties.name: Lackawanna Coal Mine Tour
properties.description: See where Santa's presents for the naughty list comes from in this tour of a 1903 coal mine.This is the last remaining mine in the Scranton region because the type of coal found in the region is no longer in high demand.

properties.name: Steamtown National Historic Site
properties.description: This railway museum is run by the National Park Service and the actual museum section features incredibly detailed history and walkthroughs of the Delaware, Lackawanna and Western Railroad. Walk through immaculately cared for railcars and see rare the Union Pacific Big Boy and DL&W MU electric commuter railcars.

properties.name: Bills Old Bike Barn
properties.description: 200+ historical motorcycles and americana in an indoor historical mockup of a fictional town called Billville.

properties.name: No. 9 Coal Mine and Museum
properties.description: No. 9 Coal Mine was the longest continuously operated coal mine in the world, running from 1855 to 1972. During the mine tour you will dive 700ft below groud beneath a mountain to an oddly drippy anthracite coal mine. If the mine seems unsafe, well now you know why they invented strip mining.

properties.name: Ringing Rocks County Park
properties.street: Ringing Rocks Rd, Upper Black Eddy, PA 18972
properties.description: Get out your hammer and start smacking rocks in the rock field to hear the funny sounds they make at Ringing Rocks State Park. The rocks sound like bells when struck, it's really unique. Its a field full of people hitting rocks with hammers. Nature.

properties.name: Dorney Park
properties.description: Dorney Park (est. 1884) is the 5th oldest amusement park in the nation. It's also home to Demon Drop - the most inhuman and terrifying ride ever constructed. Featuring 8 rollercoasters, the best waterpark in the region, and a miniature railway from the 1930s whose cattlepen like locking cars are charming and a fire hazard.

properties.name: Reading Pagoda
properties.description: A 1908 Japanese Pagoda looms over the valley of Reading, Pennsylvania. This just goes to show that Americans have always been obsessed with Japan.

properties.name: Valley Forge National Historical Park
properties.description: Valley Forge was the Continental Army's winter quarters during the winter of 1777-1778. During the winter here, Prussian military officer Friedrich von Steuben drilled the inexperienced militia until it was modeled after the most advanced military power in Europe - Prussia itself. At the park, you can witness the terrible housing conditions and fortifications that the Continental Army posessed and marvel at the fact they survived the winter at all.

properties.name: USS New Jersey
properties.description: The WW2 era Iowa-class USS New Jersey is one of the most powerful battleships the United States ever fielded. The USS New Jersey fought in WW2, Korea, Vietnam, Lebanon, and the Persian Gulf. The massive warship is now available for tour in New Jersey.

properties.name: Independence Seaport Museum
properties.street: 211 S Christopher Columbus Blvd, Philadelphia, PA 19106
properties.description: The Independence Seaport Museum features the USS Olympia - the only surviving American vessel from the Spanish-American war- and the WW2 era Balao-class submarine USS Becunana, and an indoor replica of the 1797 Schooner Dilligence.

properties.name: Museum of the American Revolution
properties.description: USA! USA! USA! Ok, the chant didn't exist yet because the 13-Colonies hadn't signed the constitution - but come see the greatest collection of American Revolution artifacts and paintings in the same city where independence was declared

properties.name: Independence Hall
properties.description: Come see the compact place where the Declaration of Independence (1776) and the United States Constitution (1787) were both argued into existence by the founding fathers of the United States. The Liberty Bell is stored just across the street.

properties.name: Mutter Museum
properties.description: Horrifying anatomical specimens and equipment that will make you go "Wow that's President Grover Cleveland's tumor". Also on site is half of Albert Einstein's brain, 139 skulls, and bones from people that had syphilus.

properties.name: Gettysburg National Military Park
properties.description: This is THE battlefield to see in the USA. The battlefield is preserved exactly as it was during the U.S. Civil War in 1863, where 185,000 soldiers fought and 36,000 died on three days in July of 1863. The battlefield features expensive monuments, and interesting landscape - in particular the Devil's Den and Little Roundtop. The visitor center features an excellent explanation of the battle, the Gettysburg Address, and an impossibly large painting of the battle called the Cyclorama

properties.name: Railroad Museum of Pennsylvania
properties.description: This railroad museum focuses on all the railroads in Pennsylvania. - and features over 100 locomotives and railcars. Prominent locomotives include the streamlined electric GG1, a B1 yard switcher, an 1838 Rocket, and the 1940's World's Fair replica of the John Bull.

properties.name: National Watch and Clock Museum
properties.description: So many interesting clocks that you'll lose track of time. Horology is just as fun as the way it's pronounced would imply.

properties.name: The Hershey Story Museum
properties.description: The closest we will ever come to Willy Wonka's chocolate factory in real life. Hershey, Pennsylvania's entire economy is devoted to this chocolate manufacturer - and the amusement park owned by the chocolate manufacturer.

properties.name: Hersheypark
properties.description: This candy themed amusement park really feels like what would have been built if Willy Wonka was an American. It's also the largest amusement park on the U.S. East Coast, with 15 different rollercoasters that are all somehow good.

properties.name: Paterson Great Falls National Historical Park
properties.description: Paterson Falls is a 77ft waterfall in a gorge in the middle of the historic industrial town of Paterson, New Jersey. The bridge, obeservation deck, and park lets you get particularly close to it.

properties.name: Paterson Museum
properties.description: The inventor of the modern submarine - John Philip Holland- has his first boats located here, including the Holland I - Holland's first submarine, and the   Fenian Ram - the world's first practical submarine. There's also guns on display from the founding of the firearms manufacturer Colt, and silk production equipment.  Call before visiting, the museum sometimes shuts down due to high internal temperatures.

properties.name: Sterling Hill Mining Museum
properties.description: Sterling Hill Mine's rocks are known for their fluorescence - they glow in the dark. Under UV light, the mine lights up into a psychedellic frenzy in the Rainbow Tunnel.

properties.name: Gateway National Recreation Area
properties.description: The Gateway to New York Harbor is strewn with abandoned WW2 era gun emplacements and other massive forifications protecting NYC. Gateway National Recreation Area is divided into three parts, each containing its own forts and beaches - Sandy Hook Unit with Fort Hancock, State Island Unit with Fort Wadsworth, and Jamaica Bay Unit with Fort Tilden.

properties.name: Matchbox Road Museum
properties.description: One man has wisely hoarded every Matchbox toy car. Tours by appointment only.

properties.name: Fort Delaware State Park
properties.description: This War of 1812 era fort has also acted as a prisoner of war camp, and is surrounded by a moat and a river - giving the impression of a castle. The fort is only accessible by boat.

properties.name: Air Mobility Command Museum
properties.description: How the heck does the most powerful military on earth move stuff around by air? This museum features basically every model of U.S.A. airlifter aircraft - all 35 of them- and yes, you can go inside many of them.

properties.name: Cape Henlopen State Park
properties.description: You know you want to wander around WW2 observation towers, forts, and gun emplacements on the beautiful beaches of Delaware.

properties.name: Coastal Wilds
properties.description: You can swim with sea otters, feed a sloth (if he feels like it), and pet capybaras at Coastal Wilds. The otters are playful and aggressive with short attention spans. One otter bit by finger here and started spinning to try to tear it off, it was adorable.

properties.name: Museum of the Bible (DC)
properties.description: Arts and crafts retail store Hobby Lobby funded the terrorist group ISIS to buy artifacts from smugglers for this museum. The artifacts were returned, but this museum dedicated to the history of how the bible as we know it came to be remains.

properties.name: International Spy Museum
properties.description: Turns out the capitol of the United States is a really good place to spy on stuff. Cold War era spying and gadgets are all here at the International Spy Museum: suicide pins, enigma machines, heavy water, forgery printing plates, buttonhole cameras, lipstick pistols, and the Aston Martin DB5 from James Bond.

properties.name: Fords Theatre
properties.description: Watch the hit 1860's play My American Cousin at the same place it was held when C-List actor John Wilkes Booth assassinated President Abraham Lincoln during the funniest joke in the play. It's also a well preserved historical theater and museum.

properties.name: National Air and Space Museum
properties.description: The USA invented flight, broke the sound barrier, and went to the moon - come see all of the actual historical aircraft that acomplished these feats first at the National Air and Space Museum on the National Mall. Including the 1903 Wright Flyer, The Spirit of St. Louis, the Bell X-1, Apollo 11's command capsule Columbia, and SpaceShipOne. There's also the original scale model of the Enterprise from Star Trek.

properties.name: National Postal Museum
properties.description: Nothing stops the mail. The US Postal Service actsas the USA's primary delivery service even when there was nothing but barren frontier and sewed the nation together. See postal wagons, trucks, trains, planes, and stamps that will make you want to go postal.

properties.name: United States Botanical Garden
properties.description: The United States Botanical Garden features exotic plants divided into rooms modeled after their native biomes. This is one of the best kept botanical gardens in the world - after all, it's right next to the United States Congress.

properties.name: National Museum of the United States Navy
properties.description: The world's most powerful navy deserves an equally powerful museum. The museum features a naval railway gun, a Vietnam era Swift Boat, and the bathysphere Trieste - the first submarine to reach the bottom of the Marianas Trench. A new museum is under construction, and you need to register for a base access pass form if you even want to do a private tour - but it's still a nice museum.

properties.name: Washington Monument
properties.description: The Washington Monument opened as the tallest structure in the world in 1884 until supassed by the Eiffel Tower. The massive obelisk is towers over the DC area.

properties.name: Lincoln Memorial
properties.street: 2 Lincoln Memorial Cir NW, Washington, DC 20002
properties.description: A massive statute of President Abraham Lincoln looms over the nationa's capitol in a memorial that echos the design of ancient Greek temples. The undercroft is nearly 8 stories deep as a necessary foundation for the swampy ground beneath.

properties.name: National Archives Building
properties.description: This is the location of the real National Treasure. The National Archives Museum is home to the original copies of the Declaration of Independence, the Constitution, the Bill of Rights, and the Emancipation Proclamation. These documents formed the foundation of the United States and have been widely copied the world over. Notably, nearly every other constitution worldwide leaves out the bits where freedom is considered more important than order - I'm sure that won't lead to problems in those countries.

properties.name: Mount Vernon
properties.street: 3200 Mount Vernon Memorial Hwy, Mt Vernon, VA 22121
properties.description: The museum, residence, plantation, distilery, and tomb of the USA's first President: George Washington. Yes you can buy the alcohol from the distillery and get hammered like Washington would have wanted.

properties.name: National Museum of the Marine Corps
properties.description: Did you know the U.S. Navy has its own army? From the Hall of Montezuma to the shores of Tripoli, the United States marines have been invading countries - and winning- since the nation's founding. Get a depressingly realistic look at the Marine's history - including a room that simulates the -54F cold of the Battle of the Chosin Reservoir  - and see the flag from Iwo Jima.

properties.name: Steven F. Udvar-Hazy Center
properties.street: 14390 Air and Space Museum Pkwy, Chantilly, VA 20151
properties.description: The National Air and Space Museum continues at the Steven F. Udvar-Hazy Center, featuring some of America's greatest aircraft that couldn't quite fit anywhere else but a hangar. Featuring the Space Shuttle Discovery, Enola Gay- the first aircraft to drop an atomic bomb, an SR-71 Blackbird,  the Concorde, the Bell XV-15, Langley Aerodrome A, Dornier Do 335, X-35 prototype for the F-35, as well as other aircraft that are the last of their model.

properties.name: NRA National Firearms Museum
properties.description: Guns, guns, and more guns - it's 3000 guns in a museum run by gun lobbyists near the capitol of the country known for its guns. See the history of the development of American guns as well as notable guns known for their shootiness.

properties.name: Manassas National Battlefield Park
properties.description: How hard could it be to win a Civil War? Just defeat the Confederate Army and march to their capitol in Richmond. See the battlefield where the Union lost against the Confederacy twice. The landscape remains the nearly the same as it was when the battles were faught in 1860 and 1862 - just some farmer's fields.

properties.name: Glen Echo Park (Maryland)
properties.description: This glitzy Art-deco amusement park is now just a regular park.

properties.name: Great Falls (Potomac River)
properties.description: A series of jagged rapids and picturesque waterfalls drops the Potomac River 76ft through a scenic gorge just north of DC.

properties.name: Patuxent River Naval Air Museum
properties.street: 22156 Three Notch Rd, Lexington Park, MD 20653
properties.description: Patuxent River Naval Air Museum is home to the X32-B and X35-C - the losing and winning fighters of the Joint Strike Fighter competition, as well as a large assortment of historical US Naval jet Aircraft and helicopters. It's the closest you'll ever be able to get to some of these airplanes, because there are no fences stopping you in the outdoor section.

properties.name: N.S. Savannah
properties.description: The world's first commercial nuclear-powered vessel was built with the interiors of an ultra-futuristic yacht to promote nuclear power to the public. Tours are only monthly or if you donate a lot of money so plan ahead.

properties.name: SS John W. Brown
properties.description: During World War II the United States initiated the Emergency Shipbuilding Program to mass-produce ships the same way automobiles had been mass produced. 2,710 Liberty Ships were produced, and the SS John W. Brown is one of two that remains operational.

properties.name: Historic Ships In Baltimore
properties.description: Baltimore merged nearly all of its maritime museums into one single massive musuem featuring: USS Constellation (1853) - the last purely sailing vessel produced by the United States Navy, the Treasury-class cutter WHEC-37 - the last surviving warship of Pearl Harbor, the WW2 era Tench-class submarine USS Torsk, the Lightship Chesapeake, and the lighthouse Seven Foot Knoll Light.

properties.name: National Aquarium (Baltimore)
properties.description: They've got so many sharks and also 750 other species of enjoyable sealife across two piers and six levels.

properties.name: Fort McHenry National Monument
properties.description: Fort McHenry resisted British bombardment during the war of 1812, preventing an invasion of Baltimore. The Star Spangled banner - the national anthem of the United States - was inspired by the never wavering flag of the United States during the intense artillery and rocket barrage. The fort itself is now available for tour.

properties.name: B&O Railroad Museum
properties.description: The Baltimore and Ohio Railroad was the oldest railroad in the United States, and the first to adopt steam engines as common carriers for its services. The line operated from 1828 until its 1987 merger with CSX. The museum features the Tom Thumb - a replica of the first American-built steam locomotive in regular service, the 1832 Grasshopper - one of the oldest surviving American locomotives, and the 1836 John Hancock.

properties.name: System Source Computer Museum
properties.description: Tour computing from its inception as mechanical tabulators to modern computers. Located right next to the National Electronics Museum.  Tours by appointment only.

properties.name: Antietam National Battlefield
properties.description: The battle Antietam during the U.S. Civil War was the site of the bloodiest one day battle in American history - 22,727 soldiers were turned into dead or casualties in 12 hours. Antietam marked the end of the Confederacy's invasion of Maryland and the victory was soon followed with the Emancipation Proclamation - ending the legal status of slavery in the Confederacy.

properties.name: Harpers Ferry National Historical Park
properties.description: On October 16th, 1859 American abolitionist John Brown raided a federal armor in Harpers Ferry with the hopes of igniting and arming a slave revolt to end slavery in the United States. The raid and resulting outpouring of sympathy for abolition during Brown's publicized trial fueled slaveowners fears that the northern states planned to end slavery by force if neccesary. The armory is now availible for tour, andthe mountains surrounding Harpers Ferry have hiking trails that enable good views of the meeting of the confluence of the Potomac and Shenandoah rivers.

properties.name: Death Valley National Park
properties.description: Death Valley is the hottest place on Earth. Around 4 people die per year in death valley due to the heat - with an average daily high of 126F in July. To be clear - it is hot, hotter than you imagine. Go during the winter, bring water, and only hike by the roads. Otherwise enjoy the colorful desert sands.

properties.name: Scottys Castle
properties.description: What better place than to build a mansion than Death Valley? Scotty's Castle is nowhere near any civilization but still manages to have eletrical power due to hydroelectic power attached to an underground spring. Part of Death Valley National Park, Scotty's Castle requires a reservation for a tour due to ongoing cleanup efforts from flooding- call ahead.

properties.name: Bodie State Historic Park
properties.description: 8000 people lived here in 1879, now 0 do. A real gold-rush era ghost town in the desert. Tour the gold mills, saloons, churches, deserted streets, and abandoned vehicles of Bodie, California.

properties.name: Fort Ross State Historic Park
properties.description: Russian colonization of the Americas reached its furthest southern point in the with the establishment of Fort Ross in 1812. Fort Ross was created in pursuit of the fur-trade and feeding the Alaskan colonies - which both rapidly declined due to over-hunting. Tour the only example of colonial Russian architecture next to the scenic California coastline.

properties.name: Maritime Museum of San Diego
properties.street: 1492 N Harbor Dr, San Diego, CA 92101
properties.description: Usually a maritime museum consists of just one ship with historical/cultural importance. The Maritime Museum of San Diego has 10; including: Star of India - the oldest iron-hulled merchant ship in the world, the San-Francisco ferryboat Berkeley, steam yacht Medea, and the diesel submarine of the US Navy - the Cold War era research submarine USS Dolphin. Replicas include: the schooner Californian, HMS Suprise, and the San Salvador - the first European explorer ship to reach San Diego. The aircraft carrier nearby, that's a different maritime museum.

properties.name: USS Midway Museum
properties.street: 910 N Harbor Dr, San Diego, CA 92101
properties.description: The WW2-era Midway-class aircraft carrier USS Midway was the longest serving aircraft carrier of the US Navy (1945-1992). The hangars and decks are now a museum for the aircraft that served on the carrier. Featuring the filming location and actual aircraft from the film Top Gun: Maverick.

properties.name: Belmont Park (San Diego)
properties.description: The Big Dipper opened in 1925 at this beachside park in sunny California and has been operating for over 100 years. I rode the Big Dipper 23 times in a row, so yes - it's good.

properties.name: Big Bend National Park
properties.street: 142 Chisos Basin Rd, Big Bend National Park, TX 79834
properties.description: In the Chihuahuan desert in dry West Texas there lays a massive circle of mountains that open upon the Rio Grande like gates to reveal an oasis of green at Big Bend National Park. The Santa Elena Canyon overlook provides the view that you have to see at the far South End of the park

properties.name: Big Bend Ranch State Park
properties.description: Every National Park has a state park right alongside it that is nearly as beautiful, but not as popular. Big Bend Ranch State Park is the state park version of Big Bend National Park. Featuring hiking through deep volcanic and limestone canyons - bring water, you are in the desert.

properties.name: Natural Tunnel State Park
properties.description: This cave was so big they put a rail line through it with little alteration. It looks like something out of a train set. The bowl shaped gorge has nearly vertical cliffs, making the arch of the tunnel even more impressive looking.

properties.name: Virginia Museum of Transportation
properties.description: The Virginia Museum of Transportation features historical locomotives that operated on the Chesapeake Western, Virginia Central, and Norfolk and Western rail lines. This includes a streamlined train called the No.611, and a Jupiter nuclear missile for some reason. I do not know why a train museum has a nuclear missile.

properties.name: Natural Bridge State Park (Virginia)
properties.street: 6477 S Lee Hwy, Natural Bridge, VA 24578
properties.description: This 215ft tall natural bridge is actually used as a bridge for U.S. Route 11. This bridge was surveyed by a young George Washington - he even engraved his initials on the site. You can hike down to the bottom of the near vertical gorge and look straightup and feel uneasy that there are cars moving above you held up only by what nature has provided.

properties.name: Natural Chimneys Regional Park
properties.street: 94 Natural Chimneys Ln, Mt Solon, VA 22843
properties.description: 120ft limestone chimney like spires loom off the side of a cliff. The Hall of Fame Jousting Tournament is held annually at the base of the chimneys.

properties.name: Shenandoah Valley National Park
properties.description: Shenandoah Valley National Park is home of Skyline Drive - where you literally drive on top of a mountain ridge while having stunning views on either side. There's waterfalls and tunnels and crazy views - and you don't even have to get out of you car. It's what George Washington would have wanted probably.

properties.name: Luray Caverns
properties.description: Luray caverns is a massive underground cave underground, but a hedge maze, toy museum, automobile museum, and living history village on the surface. The underground caverns feature rooms over 140ft tall.

properties.name: Monticello
properties.description: Thomas Jefferson authored the declaration of Independence, founded the Democratic party, and was elected President of the United States because John Adams was super condescending and unlikeable. Jefferson promptly declared war on the Barbary Pirates, doubled the size of the nation with the Louisiana Purchase, and embargoed the British to bring manufacturing back to the United States. Thomas Jefferson was a prolific inventor and architect: that swivel chair you're sitting in? Thomas Jefferson invented it. Thomas Jefferson's architectural design submission for the White House didn't win, but he built his own house at his plantation in the same style.

properties.name: James Madison's Montpelier
properties.description: James Madison authored the Bill of Rights that forms the backbone of codified freedom in the United States of America . The Bill of Rights has has been copied often, but never duplicated because other countries prioritze order over freedom - and that always works out for them. After being elected President, Madison promptly started the War of 1812, created the Second Bank of the United States, and implemented tariffs to bring industry back to the United States (are you sensing a historical theme?). James Madison's plantation is now a museum about everything James Madison.

properties.name: Appomattox Court House National Historical Park
properties.description: General George Armstrong Custer's calvary blocked the retreat of Confederate General Robert E. Lee - trapping his army at Appomatox Court House. This lead to the surrender of the Army of Northern Virginia, and as a result the end of the end of the U.S. Civil War and Slavery in the United States. The site of Lee's surrender has been reconstructed so you can relive the moment the aristocratic slaveowning traitors finally realized they had lost to a drunk guy from Ohio.

properties.name: Air Force Armament Museum
properties.description: Bombs - the sequel to planes. Come see the bomb museum. Featuring the MOAB - the largest conventional bomb in the United States' arsenal, Tomahawk Cruise Missiles, T-12 Cloudmaker Earthquake Bomb, and the BLU-82B Daisy Cutter. Outdoor aircraft including the Canberra, B-52, B-47,  SR-71 Blackbird, and 31+ other aircraft that drop bombs or find out where bombs should be dropped.

properties.name: National Naval Aviation Museum
properties.description: This is THE naval aviation museum. It only took 12 years from the invention of the aircraft to begin launching them from ships to attack other ships. The National Naval Aviation Museum is devoted to naval aviation and features 150+ aircraft including those from the Blue Angels - the Navy's Flight Demonstration Squadron (they do airshows). The museum features a control car from a navy K-class blimp, a PB2Y-5R Coronado, Curtiss NC-4, Martin Marlin, and other seaplanes and carrier aircraft tracing the history of naval aviation.

properties.name: Fort Pickens
properties.street: 1400 Fort Pickens Rd, Pensacola Beach, FL 32561
properties.description: Fort Pickens was one of the few forts in the South that did not fall into Confederate hands during the U.S. Civil War. Now you can roam the abandoned fort and WW2 gun emplacements on the beach as part of the Gulf Islands National Seashore

properties.name: Fort Morgan State Historic Site
properties.description: Do you like roaming through hurricane-damaged brick forts from the War of 1812 and WW2 artillery batteries on the beach? Of course you do.

properties.name: Fort Gaines
properties.description: Roam across the beach and through a hurricane-damaged Civil War era fort on an island while staring across the bay at a completely difference hurricane-damaged War of 1812 era fort.

properties.name: Battleship Memorial Park
properties.description: The United States has the last battleships afloat because all other nations were too poor or too naughty to keep theirs. Battleship Memorial Park is home to the WW2 era South Dakota-class battleship USS Alabama, the WW2 era Gato-class submarine USS Drum, and some random tanks and aircraft scattered around for good measure.

properties.name: United States Army Aviation Museum
properties.description: This is THE helicopter museum with over 160 aircraft (mostly helicopters). Rare museum features include: the experimental helicopters XH-51A, AH-56 Cheyenne (it had a tail thrusting propeller!), the RAH-66 Comanche (the stealth helicopter!); the convertiplanes XV-1, XV-5, VZ-3; and the compound helicopter S-72. This museum is on a military base, so you will have to go through a military checkpoint - plan ahead, call ahead.

properties.name: Noccalula Falls Park
properties.description: This 90ft waterfall features a seemingly endless overhang into a hikeable gorge. It also features a statue depicting a woman throwing herself into the gorge - which is a daring example to set for children.

properties.name: Southern Museum of Flight
properties.description: This museum features a B-25 pulled from a lake and a Soviet Mi-25 captured in the Libyan desert along with 100+ other aircraft. Some of the aircraft are a block away just down the road for the outdoor section of the museum.

properties.name: Barber Vintage Motorsports Museum
properties.description: George W. Barber was not merely satisfied with owning the racetrack nextdoor, he also collected 1600 racecars and motorcycles and literally stacked them. They are stacked on a  4-story shelf, you'll know it when you see it.

properties.name: Sloss Furnaces
properties.description: You want to run around a 15-acre abandoned steel mill from 1971 - it's just something you want to do.

properties.name: Majestic Caverns
properties.description: Majestic Caverns has a really really wide and tall room where the entire ceiling is an endless forest of Stactites. There's also a laser light show.

properties.name: U.S. Space and Rocket Center
properties.description: If you like rocket engines, this is the museum. Redstone Arsenal in Huntsville is where rocket engines actually get developed and built. As a result, the US Space and Rocket Center has a lot of rockets that you very much want to see, including an upright mockup of the Saturn V, an actual Saturn V on its side Saturn I, various space capsules and rockets, and the Space Shuttle test simulator Pathfinder

properties.name: Cathedral Caverns State Park
properties.description: This cavern is known for its stalagmites that rise from the floor like a cathedral.

properties.name: Nauticus (Norfolk)
properties.description: Norfolk is home of Naval Station Norfolk - the largest naval station in the world which protects the entrance to the USA's capitol and Chesapeake Bay. The WW2 era Iowa-class battleship USS Wisconsin is docked at Nauticus at a part of the Hampton Roads Naval Museum.  The USS Wisconsin is one of the largest battleships ever constructed, and one of the largest ever built. The USS Wisconsin served in WW2, Korea, and the Gulf War - and is now available for tour. It's really really big so it may take some time.

properties.name: The Mariners Museum and Park
properties.description: The Mariner's Museum and Park is home to the USS Monitor center. The USS Monitor was a revolutionary warship which was the first to feature a combination of complete iron armor, exclusively use of steam power, and emphasis on high caliber guns in revolving turrets. After the ironclad CSS Virginia destroyed 3 union wooden warships with impunity at the Battle of Hampton Roads in 1861 it was engaged by the USS Monitor where the two ironclad warships were unable to damage each other - marking the end of the age of sail and wooden warships forever. The museum features a full-scale replica of the USS Monitor, as well as the turret of the actual USS Monitor.

properties.name: U.S. Army Transportation Museum
properties.description: How do you move the deadliest army in the world by land? See how army logistics shifted from horses to rail to trucks and aircraft.  Including a flying car - the Curtiss-Wright Model 2500 Air-Car, the airgeep, the only surviving Vietnam era gun truck, Viet Cong bicycles ,army trains, and tank transporting trailers. You will need to pass through a military checkpoint - so plan ahead.

properties.name: Yorktown Battlefield
properties.description: See where the Continental Army and French forces besieged the British Army at Yorktown into surrender - leaving the British position in the 13 Colonies untenable, and ending the American Revolutionary War. The redoubts of the siege lines remain in place so you can walk the historical battlefield as it was - minus the massive military encampments. Yorktown Battlefield is part of the wider Colonial National Historical Park

properties.name: Busch Gardens Europe
properties.description: Supermodel Fabio got hit in the face by a goose while riding a rollercoaster here. See what an American's idea of what Europe is at this well regarded amusement park - featuring the iconic interlocking loops of the Loch Ness Monster Rollercoaster.

properties.name: Colonial Williamsburg
properties.street: 500 E Duke of Gloucester St, Williamsburg, VA 23185
properties.description: Colonial Williamsburg depicts the Colony of Virginia's capitol Williamsburg as it was during the 18th century after the hardship of initial colonization had passed. This is where humanities majors end up pretending to have a job. Notable buildings include the Capitol Building and Governor's Palace.

properties.name: Fort Monroe National Monument
properties.description: Fort Monroe is the largest fort by area ever built by the United States. It is so big that you drive your car around inside of it to get around. Fort Monroe was a beacon of freedom during the U.S. Civil War as it remained in Union control despite being surrounded by the Confederacy. Thousands of slaves from the surrounding Virginia countryside their freedom and fled to Fort Monroe. Confederacy President Jefferson Davis was imprisoned at Fort Monroe following the end of the Civil War.

properties.name: Keystone Truck and Tractor Museum
properties.street: 880 W Roslyn Rd, Colonial Heights, VA 23834
properties.description: This is THE tractor museum. One man has amassed the world's largest tractor collection - instead of endless fields of corn, it's an endless warehouse of tractors. Historical tractors, streamlined tractors, German Tractors, French Tractors, big tractors, small tractors - TRACTORS TRACTORS TRACTORS. There's also trucks.

properties.name: Petersburg National Battlefield
properties.description: The end of the U.S. Civil War descended into trench warfare as Union forces besieged the Confederate capitol of Richmond for 9 months beginning in 1864. Innovative attempts were made to break Confederate lines, including digging a tunnel beneath their position and detonating a staggering amount of explosives in it. The crater and trenchworks are still visible to this day.

properties.name: American Civil War Museum
properties.description: Richmond, Virginia was the capitol of the Confederacy during the U.S. Civil War, and the Tredegar Iron Works was the heart of industrial military production for the traitors - supplying half of all domestic production of artillery and nearly all locomotives. The decaying Iron Works are now the American Civil War museum where it's everything Civil War all the time always.

properties.name: Science Museum of Virginia
properties.description: Richmond's former railway station has been converted into a giant science museum - because no one takes trains anymore - cars forever! Also home to the submarine Aluminaut - which helped recover lost hydrogen bombs off Spain in 1966, and an SR-71 Blackbird. They also have taught rats to play basketball and have daily shows. You can also play air hockey against a robot arm.

properties.name: Strategic Air Command and Aerospace Museum
properties.description: Strategic Air Command was a command of the United States Air Force from 1947-1992 in charge of nuclear weapons, reconnaisance, and aerial refueling. SAC was based in Nebraska, and that's why this museum features: A B-36 the largest bomber ever built, an Avro Vulcan, an XF-85 Goblin, B-1 Lancer, the X-38, and the nuclear missiles Atlas, Thor, and so much more!

properties.name: Omahas Henry Doorly Zoo and Aquarium
properties.description: This is consistently rated as the world's best zoo. They have hyraxes.

properties.name: Freedom Park (Omaha)
properties.description: When you think "the ocean" and "navy" I know you think of "Omaha, Nebraska". Nonetheless, there WW2 era Admirable-class minesweeper USS Hazard and cold war era T-1-class training submarine USS Marlin are here, on dry land, 800 miles from the ocean.

properties.name: Museum of American Speed
properties.description: The Museum of American Speed is dedicated to car racing, not any particular style of racing, just racing itself. That means speedcars, go-karts, indy cars, soap box derby cars., and cars that are just jet engines with wheels attached.

properties.name: Pioneer Village (Nebraska)
properties.description: Successful plastic manufacturer Harold Warp decided to buy anything with American historical signifigance, and began collecting buildings, art, and technology with the result being: Pioneer Village a museum of museums for Great Plains Americana. Pioneer Village is spread over 28 buildings on 20acres, including a car museum of 350+ cars and covered wagons, tractors, trains, airplanes, America's oldest carousel, carriages, and so so much more.

properties.name: Ashfall Fossil Beds State Historical Park
properties.description: 12 million years ago, a volcano erupted and the prehistoric creatures at this site died from inhaling volcanic ash. The fossils of these creatures lays in a twisted pile of agony - also known as a fossil site. Now you can view these fossils up close where they lay.

properties.name: Smith Falls State Park
properties.description: This waterfall in the Great Plains pumps out of a natural spring into a verdant and narrow canyon. If the viewing platform isn't majestic enough for you, there are stairs right to the base of the falls.  Smith Falls is the highest waterfall in the state of Nebraska.

properties.name: Chimney Rock National Historic Site
properties.description: Chimney Rock is a spire of sandstone and ash that rises 286ft above the plains surrounding it. The spire was a landmark for settlers heading west as it was the first hint of mountains as they passed through the Great Plains. The spire used to be 490ft tall when it was first sighted, but has since been struck by lightning.  Visitors can hike up to the base and then look straight up to truly understand how monumental it really is.

properties.name: Scotts Bluff National Monument
properties.description: An 800ft tall castle shaped bluff towers over the flat landscape surrounding it. Tunnels and trails criss cross their way to the top of the bluff. Or you can just drive to the summit - this is America.

properties.name: Wildcat Hills State Recreation Area
properties.description: The rocky escarpment of the Wildcat Hills provides scenic view of the plains and is a perfect representation of the American West. It's all scenic buttes all the time if you can't get enough Nebraska butte.

properties.name: Toadstool Geologic Park
properties.description: It really looks like Badlands National Park except smaller and someone stacked plates of rock on everything so they resembled toadstools.

properties.name: Fort Robinson State Park
properties.description: Fort Robinson was a fort of the Old West that is towered over by hikeable tree covered badlands and bluffs. Fort Robinson was also the location of the surrender of the Lakota war leader Crazy Horse, and the 1879 Fort Robinson Massacre where Cheyenne fleeing imprisonment were hunted down and killed.

properties.name: Chadron State Park
properties.description: See sweeping badlands and buttes of the Pine Ridge escarpment from horseback or on foot. Chadron State Park was Nebraska's first state park

properties.name: Richard Nixon Presidential Library and Museum
properties.street: 18001 Yorba Linda Blvd, Yorba Linda, CA 92886
properties.description: Richard Nixon leveraged his anti-communist credentials into being the Vice President for Eisenhower during the 1950s Red Scare, was almost murdered by protestors in Venezuela,  lost to a pretty boy from Massaschusetts in the 1960 presidential election, and lost the 1962 California gubernatorial election. Undettered, Nixon learned about the magic of 'branding' and 'Silent Majorities' and won the 1968 Presidential election. As President, Nixon ended the draft, ended the Vietnam war, lowered the voting age to 18, ended the gold standard, split Communist China from the Soviet Union, signed nuclear arms limitations treaties, created the EPA, created OSHA, oversaw the moon landing, and covered up a break in to his opponent's offices leading to his resignation. He's only remembered for the last thing though.

properties.name: Oregon Dunes National Recreation Area
properties.description: 40 miles of ever shifting 500ft windswept sandstones and quicksand next to lush seasonal rainforests on the Oregon coast.

properties.name: Ecola State Park
properties.description: Seastacks, temperate rainforests, beaches, and cliffs are why Ecola State Park was the filming location for The Goonies.

properties.name: Oregon Maritime Museum
properties.description: The 1947 sternwheeler tugboat Portland was the last sternwheel tugboat built in the United States and is now a maritime museum.

properties.name: Oregon Museum of Science and Industry
properties.description: The Cold War era Barbel-class submarine is also docked here and available for tour. The rest of the museum is mostly for kids, so just buy the ticket for the submarine.

properties.name: Oregon Rail Heritage Center
properties.description: They have the orange one!!! To be more specific it's the Art Deco streamlined Southern Pacific 4449 - Daylight; part of the American Freedom Train during the Bicentennial Celebration. This is one of the most beautiful locomotives ever built - and yes you can ride in it.

properties.name: Jamestown Settlement
properties.description: English colonists landed at Jamestown in 1607 and created the first permanent English settlement in the Americas. Turns out building a colony is hard, and 75% of them died the first year. Shortly thereafter, Tobacco was established as a cash-crop and the colony prospered. Thank you smoking. Jamestown Settlement is a living history museum is a recreation of the original settlement and colony ships Susan Constant, Godspeed, and Discovery. See what it was like to try to fulfill the dream of home ownership for 17th century English settlers.

properties.name: Oregon Caves National Monument and Preserve
properties.description: The drapery formations of these caves standout because they are made of marble and reside in a temperate rainforest.

properties.name: Mount Hood National Forest
properties.street: 27500 E Timberline Road, Government Camp, OR 97028
properties.description: Mount Hood is a 11,249ft active stratovolcano home to glaciers at the summit and temperate rainforest at the base. When the mountain inevitably erupts, the mudflows will likely destroy several surrounding communities. It's also a really pretty mountain that's the tallest in the immediate area. There's skiiing and hiking if you want to take in some good views.

properties.name: Silver Falls State Park
properties.street: 20024 Silver Falls Hwy SE, Sublimity, OR 97385
properties.description: Silver Creek Canyon contains ten waterfalls with heights up to 178ft in cavernous amphiteater-like surroundings that allow trails to pass behind the water. It's much much bigger than it looks in the pictures, it's as if a building is looming over you. The 7.6 mile Trail of Ten Falls lets you see every waterfall in the park.

properties.name: Columbia River Gorge National Scenic Area
properties.description: Massive waterfalls, temperate rainforests, mountains, and hiking trails line the Colombia river as it passes through the Cascade Range to the Pacific Ocean. The highest waterfall in the area is the 620ft Multonmah falls.
