However, don't miss 242ft Wahkeena Falls, the overhanging mountain of Latourrel falls, Bridal Veil Falls, Horsetail Falls, and Ponytail falls. There's much much more to do - it's a 50 mile long gorge.

properties.name: Train Mountain Railroad
properties.description: Model railroads too small? Real railroads too big? How about 36 miles of rideable miniature railroad at Train Mountain - the largest miniature railroad in the world. Weave through the mountains of Oregon on miniature trains, and check out the rail museum for regular sized trains.

properties.name: Newberry National Volcanic Monument
properties.description: This place might not look it, but you're standing in the middle of the caldera of the largest volcano in the Cascade Volanic Arc Walk across a dead-volcano at the Lava Butte, through ancient lava tubes at Lava River Cave,  see lava molds of ancient trees at Lava Cast Forest. The grounds remain dead from ancient lava flows - and you can hike among them.

properties.name: High Desert Museum
properties.description: The eastern half of Oregon is arid steppe called the High Desert, and the High Desert Museum . Featuring re-creations of native american villages, fur trapping encampments, boomtowns, an entire sawmill, and live otters and other wildlife.

properties.name: Smith Rock State Park
properties.street: 9988 NE Crooked River Dr, Terrebonne, OR 97760
properties.description: Sheer 350ft cliffs of volcanic basalt are nearly all rock climbing destinations.

properties.name: John Day Fossil Beds National Monument
properties.description: John Day Fossil Beds National Monument is broken up into three separate units - the palisades and volcanic lahars of the Clarno Unit; the volcanic strata, fossils museum and bighorn sheep of the Sheep Rock Unit, and the colorful red sashes on wavy yellow hills of the Painted Hills Unit. Each unit is a hiking destination in its own right and are each located roughly 30 minutes from each other.

properties.name: National Historic Oregon Trail Interpretive Center
properties.description: This is THE Oregon Trail museum. Before the transcontinental railroad, America settlers drove their wagons westwards across the plains and rocky mountains towards the rich farmland of Oregon. The museum features the development of the Oregon trail as well as the remnnants of a gold mine.

properties.name: Carolina Beach State Park
properties.street: 1010 State Park Rd, Carolina Beach, NC 28428
properties.description: Venus Fly Traps come from a small section of North and South Carolina. At Carolina Beach State Park you can walk into the woods to see Venus Fly Traps via Flytrap Trail.

properties.name: USS North Carolina
properties.description: The WW2 era North Carolina-class battleship North Carolina was completed prior to WW2 and saw action in the Pacific Theater. The massive warship is the only surviving battleship concieved under the Washington Treaty System, which aimed to prevent naval arms races by limiting battleship size and caliber. The ship is a city in itself and was staffed by 2000 crew members - and now you can roam around it on self-guided tours.

properties.name: Roanoke Island Festival Park
properties.description: In 1585 the English attempted to permanently colonize North America for the first time under the leadership of Sir Walter Raleigh. When the English returned to Roanoake to resupply their colony in 1590, they found it abandoned - but didn't search for them- despite indications that the colonists had reloacted to Croatoan Island. The English did not attempt to colonize North America again for another 15 years. The Roanoake Adventure Museum chronicles the history of the 'lost colony' , an 'American Indian town', a re-creation of the settlement, and possesses a replica of the colony ship Elizabeth that was part of the attempt to colonize Roanoake Island.

properties.name: The Birthplace of Pepsi
properties.description: In 1898 pharmacist Caleb Bradham invented what is now Pepsi-Cola: the backbone of the PepsiCo food conglomerate which now encompasses 25% of the US Soft Drink market. Coca-Cola is only more successful because they put the same plants as cocaine in their drinks. See where it's everything blue and Pepsi at this museum - also the straight up just tell you the formula.

properties.name: Fort Macon State Park
properties.street: 2303 E Fort Macon Rd, Atlantic Beach, NC 28512
properties.description: Even more Civil War era forts on the beach! This one also used to be a prison. Roam around through the probably haunted masonry halls of Fort Macon, then hit the sand

properties.name: CSS Neuse
properties.description: The CSS Neuse was a Confederate ironclad warship built during the US Civil War - she was sunk by her crew before ever seeing combat. The hull was recovered, and a replica of the warship was built at the CSS Neuse Civil War Museum. Now you can wander around inside of it and wonder why they display the Confederate flag so proudly.

properties.name: Boars Nest - A Dukes of Hazzard Museum
properties.description: Have you ever been such a big fan of a television show you recreated the set as if it were a real place? Well the people at the Boar's Nest have done so for the TV show Dukes of Hazard (the show with the orange car with a confederate flag on top where they destroyed a car every episode). This is one of those museums run by a guy on Facebook, so check the web ahead of time before going.

properties.name: Airborne and Special Operations Museum
properties.description: Attacking from the sky was never a possibility in warfare until recent human history. This museum is dedicated to the crazy people who jump out of planes, helicopters, and gliders - and all the spec ops in between.

properties.name: Fort Sumter and Fort Moultrie National Monument
properties.description: Stand behind the cannons at Fort Moultrie and try not to say that Fort Sumter looks bombardable. The bombardment of Fort Sumter by the Confederacy started the U.S. Civil War - now you can tour both forts. You will need to get a tour boat to Fort Sumter though.

properties.name: Patriots Point
properties.street: 40 Patriots Point Rd, Mt Pleasant, SC 29464
properties.description: Patriots Point is home of the WW2 Essex-class aircraft carrier USS Yorkton and the WW2 era Allen M. Sumner-class destroyer USS Laffey, THE VIETNAM EXPERIENCE, and the U.S. Medal of Honor Museum. It's a million square feet of state-of-the-art 1940s technology, jets, and history that you can just kind of wander about in.

properties.name: Warren Lasch Conservation Center
properties.description: The CSS Hunley was the first submarine to ever sink another ship - it also sank itself. Come see the actual recovered submarine. Get inside of a replica of the submarine and imagine cranking the submarine forward towards your doom.  Visits are only on the weekends - so plan ahead.

properties.name: Reed Gold Mine
properties.description: The Reed Mine's discovery of gold in North Carolina kicked off the Carolina gold rush. Settlers flooded to North Carolina in a bid to strike it rich. Guided tours are now offered of the 1799 Gold Mine - one of the oldest mines in the nation.

properties.name: NASCAR Hall of Fame
properties.street: 400 E M.L.K. Jr Blvd, Charlotte, NC 28202
properties.description: Turning left has never been so fun at the NASCAR Hall of Fame. Learn about the best of the best in NASCAR history.  Featuring racing simulators, a movie theater, and so many race cars you will develop a strong desire to never take right turns again.

properties.name: Sullenberger Aviation Museum
properties.description: When else are you going to see a plane that crashed? Come see a commercial passenger plane that crashed in the Hudson River. There's also 40+ historical aircraft here too.

properties.name: Grandfather Mountain State Park
properties.description: Hike or drive to the top of a mountain to see the "Mile High Swinging Bridge" spanning a gorge between two mountains. The view from the top is spectacular, and you can keep hiking to see even more!

properties.name: Mount Mitchell State Park
properties.description: Mount Mitchell is the highest peak (6684ft) east of the Mississippi River. The good news is you can drive to the top, because America loves you. There's also a string of trails along the mountaintop if you feel like excercising.

properties.name: Biltmore
properties.description: The Vanderbilt family built the largest privately owned home (178,926sqft) in the United States in extravagant style. It's not just a mansion, he built an entire fake village, winery, gardens, lagoon, waterfall, stables, bass pond, and boathouse. It's 8000 acres of gilded age excess.

properties.name: Chimney Rock State Park
properties.street: 174 Chimney Rock Park Rd, Chimney Rock, NC 28720
properties.description: Chimney Rock is a 315ft monolith, but the park is so much more. There are 400ft tall waterfalls flowing down overhanging cliffs, hiking tunnels bored through the mountainside, and miles of scenic hiking. Reservations are required - plan ahead.

properties.name: Gorges State Park
properties.description: 26 waterfalls through rugged river gorges at the tripoint of North Carolina, South Carolina, and Georgia - all in the Appalachian Temperate Rainforest. Rainbow and Turtleback falls are especially shallow, and resemble a glass thin sheet of water rushing over the smooth bare rock of the mountainside.

properties.name: Whitewater Falls (North Carolina)
properties.description: A 411ft waterfall that's so pretty people keep going off the trail to slip and die. It's the highest waterfall east of the Rocky Mountains, and  is a part of Nantahala National Forest.

properties.name: Dry Falls (North Carolina)
properties.street: Dry Falls Parking Lot, Highlands, NC 28741
properties.description: Dry Falls is a 65ft waterfall with a viewing area beneath its overhang - meaning you are behind the waterfall itself. Dry Falls is very busy - so plan ahead - try to come here early in the morning or late in the evening.

properties.name: Ronald Reagan Presidential Library
properties.description: B-list movie star Ronald Reagan made a really good speech in support of Republican presidential nominee Barry Goldwater in 1964, which he leveraged into a successful run for Governor of California, then President. Reagan challenged the Soviet Union to an arms race it couldn't afford, leading to the dissolution of America's greatest enemy. Reagan also ignored the AIDS epidemic, ended inflation, got rid of government regulations, got shot, hid he had alzheimers, and cut taxes - leading to massive budget deficits. However, he was really charismatic, the economy was doing great, and the Soviet Union was defeated - so he was very popular. Reagan kept Air Force One for himself at this library.

properties.name: Knotts Berry Farm
properties.description: A chicken dinner restaurant leveraged its success into becoming a major amusement park. You can still get the chicken dinners, and they are delicious. The park also features the greatest log flume ride ever built, an actual ghost town, a replica of Independence Hall, and a lineup of 9 stellar rollercoasters that each try to do something unique.

properties.name: San Francisco Maritime National Historical Park
properties.street: 2984 Hyde Street Pier #2976, San Francisco, CA 94109
properties.description: Whereas most maritime museums consists of just one ship, theSan Francisco Maritime National Historical Park consists of 6. This includes the steam ferryboat Eureka, the 1886 sailing ship Balclutha, the lumber schooner C.A. Thayer, the scow schooner Alma, and the tugs Eppelton Hall and Hercules. The museum building itself is set inside an Art Deco bathhouse.

properties.name: Alcatraz Island
properties.description: Alcatraz Federal Penitentiary opened in 1934 to house the most notorious criminals of the United States - making it one of the most famous prisons in the United States. Considered nearly inescapable due to the fast ice-cold currents surrounding the island, nonethless prisoners tried their best to escape anyway. The island is situated in the middle of San Francisco Bay, giving a spectacular view of the city and surrounding area. Part of the Golden Gate National Recreation Area.

properties.name: Castle Air Museum
properties.description: This is the best air museum in California. 35 acres of 80+ historical aircraft relaxing outdoors - including the B-36 - the largest bomber ever built. Other highlights include Air Force One (VC-9), an Avro Vulcan, CF-100 Canuck, F-117 nighthawk, SR-71 Blackbird, and Saab Draken.

properties.name: California State Railroad Museum
properties.description: The California State Railroad museum traces the history of railroading in California, from the arrival of the first steam engines during the California Gold Rush to the dominance of diesel. The museum has over 25 historic locomotives in pristine condition - and they look exactly how you would expect the trains of the Wild West to look. Featuring the C.P. Huntington - the first locomotive ever bought by Central Pacific Railroad in 1863. The C.P. Huntington is also better known as the model of train that every miniature railroad in every amusement park and zoo has copied.

properties.name: Marshall Gold Discovery State Historic Park
properties.description: This is THE gold rush museum. In 1848 gold was discovered in this location, sparking the California Gold Rush. This historic park includes the ghost town of Coloma, and a museum tracing the history of the gold rush. Take gold panning lessons and see the mill where gold was first discovered, along with 20 other historic buildings.

properties.name: Santa Cruz Beach Boardwalk
properties.description: The 1924 Giant Dipper rollercoaster is still roaring at Santa Cruz Beach Boardwalk, along with a strong supporting lineup of rides and attractions that overlook the beach. Come on down to California's oldest amusement park which has stood the test of time.

properties.name: Big Basin Redwoods State Park
properties.street: 21600 Big Basin Hwy, Boulder Creek, CA 95006
properties.description: Once you hiike among Redwood trees in the wild, you will never stop thinking about how weak and tiny all other trees look in comparison.

properties.name: Computer History Museum
properties.street: 1401 N Shoreline Blvd, Mountain View, CA 94043
properties.description: See how humanity tricked rocks into thinking at the Computer History Museum. See how computing evolved from spinning gears in mechanical tabulators to shelve-sized computers to  handheld personal computing supported by shelve-sized computers. Only at the Computer History Museum.

properties.name: Winchester Mystery House
properties.street: 525 S Winchester Blvd, San Jose, CA 95128
properties.description: When you are losing your mind, but have lots of money, you too can build a 160 room mansion with a deliberately confusing floor plan to stop ghosts. Is that door real? Does that staircase go anywhere? Find out!

properties.name: USS Potomac (AG-25)
properties.description: The President used to own a yacht. It's like Yacht Force One, and it's available for tour.

properties.name: USS Hornet Sea, Air and Space Museum
properties.description: The WW2 era Essex-class aircraft carrier USS Hornet is now a museum ship that you can roam through. The Hornet saw extensive service in WW2, Vietnam, and the Space Race. The Hornet recovered Apollo 11 and 12 - and as a result the museum has dedicated space sections. Including: the Mobile Quarantine Facility, and an Apollo Command Module. There's also a bunch of carrier aircraft.

properties.name: SS Jeremiah O Brien
properties.description: The SS Jeremiah O'Brien is one of the last operational Liberty Ships afloat. During WW2 the United States embarked on a massive shipbuilding program to haul cargo across the Atlantic. The Liberty Ships were the most mass produced ship ever in history, but few remain. Tour one of the last ones! The cargo hold is a museum too.

properties.name: SS Red Oak Victory
properties.description: The WW2 era Victory ships were the sequel to the mass-produced Liberty Ships. The Red Oak Victory in particular saw service in the Pacific. It's even more WW2 era cargo ships, which there aren't a lot of. The Red Oak Victory would be much more impressive if the SS Jeremiah O'Brien weren't docked so close by. Still, it's well worth a visit.

properties.name: San Francisco Cable Car Museum
properties.description: The San Francisco Cable Cars are not propelled by onboard motors, instead they grip a continuously moving cable in the middle of the roadway propelled by a massive central motor. Come see the massive central motor, the terrifyingly tense wires, and a plethora of historical cable cars that have been plying the streets since 1878.

properties.name: Angel Island State Park
properties.description: If your family is from the west coast of the United States, there's a good chance your ancestors passed through here if they passed the disease and poverty checks. Angel island also doubled as a missile station and Prisoner of War camp. Now you too can imagine what is was like to be rejected from entering the United States after crossing the entire Pacific Ocean. Angel Island is only accessible by boat.

properties.name: Calveras Big Trees State Park
properties.description: Giant Sequoias are unbelievably massive and live for thousands of years, and only grow in a limited section of the Sierra Nevada mountains in California. These are some of the tallest trees in the world.

properties.name: RMS Queen Mary
properties.description: The RMS Queen Mary is the last surviving transatlantic passenger ship and was the fastest of its time. The interior design itself is lavish Art Deco  - and now you can enjoy it either through a tour or as a hotel. There's also a rotting Soviet Submarine inhabited by raccoons next door.

properties.name: Tule Lake National Monument
properties.description:
"What if you took everyone in America of one ethnicity and concentrated them in some kind of camp?" - President Franklin Delano Roosevelt, probably.

The United States incacerated nearly every American of Japanese Descent during WW2, stole all their property, and then gave zero compensation for their hardship after releasing them. Tule Lake was the largest camp and incarcerated 18,700 at its peak. Now you can walkthrough a portion of the camp and reflect on how many of their own values Americans will give up to 'win'.

properties.name: Lava Beds National Monument
properties.street: 1 Indian Well Campground Trail, Tulelake, CA 96134
properties.description: Don't be fooled by the lack of mountains, you're actually on top of the active Medicine Lake shield Volcano, and 26 lava tubes are now caves available for tour and exploration.

properties.name: Ocean Star Offshore Drilling Rig and Museum
properties.description: Tour a 1969 oil rig while being surrounded by other oil rigs waiting for deployment. It's also a museum which explains how offshore drilling works.

properties.name: International Petroleum Museum and Exposition
properties.description: The alligators surrounding this 1954 oil rig make it look like a James Bond villain's lair. This is the oil rig from which all modern oil rigs are descended. The world's first mobile offshore drilling rig Mr. Charlie is now a museum - it's also staggering how massive it is. It's guided tours only - so call ahead.

properties.name: San Jacinto Monument
properties.description: Texas built a 567ft art deco monument to itself to honor the battle in which Texas won its independence from Mexico. The view from the top is just oil refineries as far as the eye can see.

properties.name: Space Center Houston
properties.description: This is the "Houston" in "Houston, we have a problem". NASA's mission control is located far away from the rockets that explode sometimes. The museum features the Space Shuttle replica Independence atop the Shuttle Carrier Aircraft - and you can go inside both. There's also , numerous space capsules such as Apollo 17's Command Module America and rocket boosters such as Falcon 9, and a complete Saturn V.

properties.name: Kemah Boardwalk
properties.description: The Boardwalk Bullet rollercoaster has been crammed onto a tight plot of land and goes blazingly fast. The supporting lineup of rides is quite pleasant - including a train that goes through the tourist trap section of the boardwalk and a fake wild west town. There's also stray cats that wander the boardwalk, and they are very cute.

properties.name: Seawolf Park
properties.description: The WW2 era Gato-class submarine USS Cavalla and the WW2 era Edsall-class destroyer escot USS Stewart both sit on dry land at the mouth of Galveston Bay. The USS Cavalla is historically notable in that it sank the Japanese aircraft carrier Shokaku. Wander around and inside of both ships at the Galveston Naval Museum at Seawolf Park.

properties.name: USS Texas
properties.description: The New York-class battleship USS Texas is the last surviving dreadnought in the world. This is the oldest American battleship afloat and saw service during WW1 and WW2 - including the famous Normandy landings. It's also a great map in the video game series Call of Duty. The ship is currently undergroind major renovations, so you have to call ahead to get a guided tour.

properties.name: Oklahoma City National Memorial Museum
properties.street: 620 N Harvey Ave, Oklahoma City, OK 73102
properties.description: Before 9/11, the Oklahoma City Bombing was considered THE national tragic terrorist attack. 169 people were killed by a truck bomb which partially collapsed the Alfred P. Murrah Federal Building on April19, 1995. The museum covers the timeline of the attack and followup investigation. Now you can buy T-shirts from the museum store that say "Oklahoma City National Memorial Museum".

properties.name: National Cowboy and Western Heritage Museum
properties.description: It's a museum of everything true and false about cowboys in the Wild West. Featuring stagecoaches, stables, teepees, rodeo history, and a complete re-creation of an old west town and Native American cliff dwelling.

properties.name: Museum of Osteology
properties.street: 10301 S Sunnylane Rd, Oklahoma City, OK 73160
properties.description: Bones! The museum! This museum full of bones is the actual bones of animals still around on this planet - including humans.

properties.name: The Toy and Action Figure Museum
properties.street: 111 S Chickasaw St, Pauls Valley, OK 73075
properties.description: It's every toy that you ever saw on TV from the 1970s-1990s all in one place.

properties.name: Turner Falls
properties.description: Turner Falls is a 77ft waterfall emerging from the cliffs of the Arbuckle Mountains. You can swim up to the base. There's also a castle here for some reason.

properties.name: U.S. Army Artillery Museum
properties.description: Artillery remains king of the battlefield - causing the most casualties out of any single weapon in modern warfare. Come see the development of American artillery from muzzle loading cannons, to breech loading field guns, to modern self-proppeled artillery and rockets. Also featured in the Artillery Park is the M65 atomic cannon - a gun that shoots nuclear artillery shells. You will need to pass through a military checkpoint to enter this museum - plan accordingly - fill out the visitor pre-registration form at least 24 hours ahead of time.

properties.name: Wichita Mountains Wildlife Refuge
properties.street: Wichita Mountains Wildlife Refuge Visitor Center, OK-49 #49, Lawton, OK 73507
properties.description: Herds of bison roam freely near the slopes of Mount Scott (2,464ft) - the tallest mountain in Oklahoma. Don't worry, you can drive your car to the top of the mountain - this is America. There's a lot of hiking trails if you're interested in clambering over boulders.

properties.name: Alabaster Caverns State Park
properties.description: The Alabaster Caverns are the world's largest gypsum caverns, filled with rare Black gypsum only found in Oklahoma.

properties.name: USS Batfish
properties.description: The WW2 era Balao-class submarine USS Batfish now rests on dry land in Oklahoma. Now you can go inside it and see a bunch of other military artifacts scatted around War Memorial Park

properties.name: Philbrook Museum of Art
properties.description: An oil baron built this Italian Renaissance style mansion and stuffed it full of the best art you could buy in the 1920s.

properties.name: Woolaroc
properties.description: A 1920s oil baron decided to buy a bunch of fancy art, wildlife, and fund a plane in the 1927 Dole Air Race. Now his scenic ranch is open to tour along with his art collection.

properties.name: Wonderland Park (Texas)
properties.description: This remote amusement park is chock full of charm, including: an indoor coaster that is now outdoors, a rollercoaster with no seatbelt, and a steel rollercoaster made by a water ride manufacturer with the trains of a wooden rollercoaster manufacturer.

properties.name: Palo Duro Canyon State Park
properties.description: This is the second largest canyon in the country after the Grand Canyon. This crisp red canyon features rocky outcroppings, stacks, and hiking just like you'd find further out west. This one might be even better because you can drive to the bottom of it - take that, nature!

properties.name: Caprock Canyons State Park and Trailway
properties.street: 850 Caprock Canyon Park Road, Quitaque, TX 79255
properties.description: Rust red buttes and canyons with wild bison herds make for great hiking and sightseeing. There's also caves full of bats if you're feeling bold. Yes you can drive down to the bottom - Texas loves you.

properties.name: American Windmill Museum
properties.description: This is THE windmill museum. It's three buildings and an entire field full of 200+ windmills and millstones. Most of the windmills still spin, so it it's like being in a room full of constantly spinning wheels.

properties.name: Fort Worth Water Gardens
properties.description: Walk down the steps of this artificial cascade of waterfalls in the middle of Fort Worth. The neat thing is that if you fall in, there is no ladder back up.

properties.name: National Vietnam War Museum
properties.description: Get flashbacks to 'Nam at the National Vietnam War Museum. Pop out of rat tunnels and traumatize veterans, hop in the back of an amphibious APC, rethink your life in the contemplation garden where a helicopter roars overhead, admire the traps of the Viet Cong. There's also a re-creation of the Oval Office where you can beg for a pardon.

properties.name: International Bowling Museum
properties.description: Learn about the history of bowling, see where bowling research is conducted, and bowl at the International Bowling Museum. Did you know bowling began in Ancient Egypt? This is an actually true fact. See medieval bowling pins, learn about lawn bowling, the criminalization of bowling, the establishment of the American Bowling Congress, how pinsetting was a job for humans instead of a machine, the development of the modern bowling alley, and professional bowling in the USA.

properties.name: George W. Bush Presidential Center
properties.description: Learn why President George W. Bush did nothing wrong (in their opinion) at the George W. Bush Presidential Museum. Understand why No Child Left Behind had no negative outcomes, the tax cuts were affordable, and why the Iraq and Afghanistan wars were about defending freedom and only had positive ramifications.

properties.name: National Video Game Museum
properties.description: The National Video Game Museum chronicles the history of the development of video gaming. They have every console ever produced and nearly every game. You can check ouyt games from their library to play at the museum. Try to go early in the morning, the nerds are less sweaty then.

properties.name: The Sixth Floor Museum at Dealy Plaza
properties.description: Look out the window where Lee Harvey Oswald shot President John F. Kennedy from and realize "Wow that's not so hard". This museum is everything about the assassination of JFK, from the history of the killer, the events in Dallas, the investigation, and persisting alternative theories. Yes they have an example of the gun that was used to kill JFK.

properties.name: American Airlines C.R. Smith Museum
properties.description: Learn about the history of American Airlines and why they are the greatest airline ever. Slide down an inflatable plane escape slide, sit in economy in a DC-3, and learn why it wasn't their fault at all their planes were hijacked on 9/11.

properties.name: Southwest Dairy Museum
properties.description: This is THE dairy museum. Learn about why milk is the greatest thing ever,  how milk gets from a cow into a bottle, recipes that you can make from dairy products. A talking skeleton riding a bicycle will crack milk jokes and tell you about why calcium is great.

properties.name: Waco Mammoth National Monument
properties.description: 24 Columbian mammoths died suddenly, and their fully intact skeletons are now embedded in the stone outside of Waco Texas for all to see.

properties.name: Dr. Pepper Museum
properties.description: Dr. Pepper was invented in 1884 by Charles Alderton who started mixing carbonated beverages with the fruit syrups in the drug store he worked at. This museum is the site of the first dedicated Dr. Pepper bottling plant. At the Dr. Pepper museum you can mix your own syrups to create your own soda, go on ghost tours, learn about soda making in a laboratory, look at historic vending machines and everything related to soda production, and get a free Dr. Pepper with your admission.

properties.name: Guadalupe Mountains National Park
properties.street: V5VH+P6, 400 Pine Canyon Dr, Salt Flat, TX 79847
properties.description: The Guadalupe Mountains contain the highest point in Texas (8,751ft) which utterly dominates the flat landscape leading up to the mountains themselves. In the shadows of the valley of the mountains lay green hills and rivers that you can hike about. From the mountaintops you can look at the endless flat plain before you, emphasizing just how high up you are. This is not one of those parks you can drive through, everything you want to experience requires a fairly long hike.

properties.name: Permian Basin Petroleum Museum
properties.description: This is THE oil well museum. See the development of the oil well from derrick to pumpjack, with actual examples of each step towards today's oil extraction technology. See how oil is formed from ancient lifeforms, the chemistry behind petroleum's high energy potential, a bunch of sports cars because gasoline engines are awesome, and how the public has viewed the oil industry during its lifespan. Also there's an exhibit where they treat drilling for oil like space exploration and you get in a fake spaceship called the Petroltrekker.

properties.name: Alamo Mission
properties.description: Don't you forget it. During the Texas Revolution defenders fortified the abandoned Alamo Mission and all were executed during their surrender. Today the mission has been preserved to be as it was on the day of the battle. It's also in the middle of downtown San Antonio - literally.

properties.name: USS Lexington (CV-16)
properties.street: 2914 N Shoreline Blvd, Corpus Christi, TX 78402
properties.description: The WW2 era Essex-class aircraft carrier USS Lexington is the oldest aircraft carrier in the world. The ship is massive and contains an entire aerospace museum inside of its hangers. They also have escape rooms if people still do that.

properties.name: Six Flags Fiesta Texas
properties.description: Six Flags Fiesta Texas is set inside of a quarry, and makes use of it. Rollercoasters dive off the cliff walls, and trains pass through tunnels covered by waterfalls. There are 11 rollercoasters in total, with a strong supporting cast of rides - including the Bugs Bunny Log Flume.

properties.name: National Museum of the Pacific War
properties.description: It's World War 2, but only the bit where the USA fought the Japanese. Including a Japanese midget submarine that participated in the attack on Pearl harbor, PT-309, and an outdoor re-creation of a Pacific combat zone where reenactments are held.

properties.name: Lyndon Baines Johnson Library and Museum
properties.description: LBJ assumed the presidency after President JFK was assassinated in Dallas. LBJ went on to leverage the nation's desire to honor JFK by ramming through the Great Society programs (Medicare, Medicaid), the Voting Rights Act, the Civil Rights Act, and accelerated the US Space Program. Johnson also escalated the Vietnam war, which the youth of the nation did not appreciate since they could be drafted at age 18 but could not vote until age 21. LBJ declined to run for a second term. The LBJ Presidential Library has the presidential limousine, a terrifying talking animatronic of LBJ, and a re-creation of the oval office.

properties.name: Bullock Texas State History Museum
properties.description: Texas wants you to know why Texas is the greatest place ever. Texas has been in a near perpetual economic boom since it joined the USA due to its dominance in the fields of cattle, cotton, lumber, and oil. The museum traces the history of Texas from the Native Americans, to explorers, to settlement, independence, Civil War, to the present. They even have the entire hull of explorer Robert La Salle's ship.

properties.name: George H.W. Bush Presidential Library and Museum
properties.street: 1000 George Bush Dr W, College Station, TX 77845
properties.description: George H.W. Bush went from pilot in WW2 to Director of the CIA, to Reagan's Vice President, to President. Bush successfully oversaw the mostly peaceful dissolution of communism in Eastern Europe, passed the Americans With Disabilities Act, the North American Free Trade Agreement, the Gulf War, and raised taxes. Now you can learn the complete story of the 41st President and why he didn't do anything wrong (in their opinion).

properties.name: Cave Without A Name
properties.description: It's a really big cave with a bunch of wacky formations of stalactites, stalagmites, soda straws, drapery, flowstones, rimstone dams, and concerts in the Throne Room (a really big cavern). Call ahead - you likely need a reservation.

properties.name: Natural Bridge Caverns
properties.street: 26495 Natural Bridge Caverns Rd, San Antonio, TX 78266
properties.description: Natural Bridge Caverns are another one of those impressively large caverns filled with formations. It's so big that you have to take a series of switchbacks just to descend within one of the rooms. There's a lot of cavern to see, that's why there's two separate tours.

properties.name: Longhorn Cavern State Park
properties.street: 6211 Park Rd 4 W, Marble Falls, TX 78654
properties.description: Swooshing caverns with arches, it's the "National Cave of Texas". There's even a formation that looks exactly like a dog.

properties.name: Enchanted Rock State Natural Area
properties.description: It's a smooth mountain made of pink granite with a lake nearby that lets you reflect on the height. There's hiking, rock climbing, and boulders galore. Altogther, it's just a very pleasant place to be.

properties.name: Garner State Park
properties.description: The gentle Frio River passes by the mountains and cliffs of Mount Old Baldy. The view from the summit is quite impressive and is worth the hike. If going uphill isn't that interesting, the river is also full of interesting rock formations. There's also caves - with no guided tours.

properties.name: Caverns of Sonora
properties.description: The walls are popcorn and the floor is crystals in the curvy cave walls of the Caverns of Sonora.

properties.name: Fun Spot America Atlanta
properties.description: During COVID, this small amusement park got a discount and built the world's #10 ranked steel rollercoaster. There's almost never a line for it due to its capacity, so you can ride it over and over. There's also some great go-kart tracks.

properties.name: Rock City (Lookout Mountain)
properties.description: Rock City Gardens is a series of gardens and pathways on top of Lookout Mountain. There's chasm-spanning bridges and waterfalls with stunning views.

properties.name: Stone Mountain
properties.street: 1000 Robert E Lee Blvd, Stone Mountain, GA 30083
properties.description: Stone Mountain is Atlanta's version of Ayers Rock - it's a massive isolated igneous dome. Carved into the side of the mountan is the Confederate version of Mount Rushmore - depicting the traitors Jefferson Davis, Robert E. Lee, and Stonewall Jackon. You can hile all around the mountain and to the top - or take an aerial tramway up if you're feeling rich.

properties.name: National Prisoner of War Museum
properties.description: During the U.S. Civil War, the Confederate prisoner-of-war camp of Andersonville held Union soldiers in such deplorable conditions that 13,000 of them died. There was no food, no water, and no sanitation. The conditions were so bad that the U.S. invented the concept of charging individuals with war crimes to charge the commandant. The National Prisoner of War Museum documents the treatment of Americans as prisoners-of-war - including the horrors of Andersonville.

properties.name: Jimmy Carter National Historical Park
properties.description: Jimmy Carter turned his small hometown of Plains, Georgia into the center of his political campaigns for state senate, governor, and President. The small rail depot in town acted as campaign headquarters. Jimmy Carter's house, boyhood farm, and high school are all now part of the National Historical Park.

properties.name: Providence Canyon State Park
properties.description: Erosion from poor farming practices has formed this 150ft colorful canyon with an abandoned homestead and rusting cars at the bottom. You can hike all along the canyon - but it's slippy.

properties.name: National Infantry Museum
properties.description: This is THE U.S. army museum. Located next to a military base supporting 120,000 people, the National Infantry Museum traces the history of the U.S. Infantry with some really cool looking displays. This include re-creations of the battlefields of Yorktown, Antietam, Soissons, Omaha Beach, Corregidor, Korea, Vietnam, and Iraq. It's a really cool museum and the recruiters there would very much like it if you joined the military pretty please.

properties.name: National Civil War Naval Museum
properties.description: It's a museum of the U.S. Civil War - but only the bits on water. Featuring the wreckage of the Confederate ironclad  CSS Jackson and CSS Chattahoochee, a replica of the Union paddlewheel frigate USS Hartford, a replica of the CSS Albemarle, and a replica of the USS Monitor's turret. Sometimes they fire a cannon into the river.

properties.name: Ocmulgee Mounds National Historical Park
properties.description: Early Mississippian-culture Native Americans built 55ft tall mounds. Now you can walk to the top of and go inside them.

properties.name: Jimmy Carter Library and Museum
properties.street: 441 John Lewis Freedom Pkwy NE, Atlanta, GA 30307
properties.description: Jimmy Carter went from peanut farmer, to U.S. Navy nuclear reactor technician, to state senator, governor, then President. During his presidency gas prices doubled, causing stagflation. Carter's achievements as president include deregulation, pardoning Vietnam draft dodgers, creating the EPA Superfund site program, handing the Panama Canal over to Panama, creating peace between Israel and Egypt, and enabling fracking. Post-presidency Jimmy Carter took on humanitarian causes, including very nearly succeeded in eliminating the guinea worm. Now you can learn why Jimmy Carter did nothing wrong (in their opinion) at his Presidential Libary and Museum.

properties.name: Cumberland Island National Seashore
properties.street: Plum Orchard Dr, St Marys, GA 31558
properties.description: Roam through the ruins of burned down plantations on this sunny tropical island where wild horses roam free.

properties.name: Fort Pulaski National Monument
properties.description: Union troops tested rifled cannons by besieging this fort during the U.S. Civil War. You can still see the damages from the bombardment today - a rarity among forts in the U.S.

properties.name: Tallulah Gorge State Park
properties.street: 338 Jane Hurt Yarn Rd, Tallulah Falls, GA 30573
properties.description: Pedestrian bridges span this 1000ft gorge enabling spectacular views of 5 waterfalls. You can hike on the edge of the gorge via the Tallulah Gorge Rim Trail which actually has you walk through some of the waterfalls themselves.

properties.name: Amicalola Falls State Park
properties.description: You can get really close to this 729ft waterfall via the viewing decks and suspension bridge. There's viewing decks at the top, middle, and bottom of this seemingly endless waterfall.

properties.name: World of Coca-Cola
properties.description: If the commercials on TV didn't inform you of Coca-Cola's existence, this museum sure will. This museum traces the history of coca-cola from when it had cocaine in it to the world's largest soft-drink manufacturer. It's the corporate propaganda you know you crave. They even serve the flavors they only sell overseas here, as well as 'New Coke'.

properties.name: Georgia Aquarium
properties.description: This is THE aquarium. Georgia Aquarium has whale sharks - the largest fish in existence. This aquarium is by far the best aquarium in the U.S. and one of the best in the entire world. They have giant manta rays,  hammerhead sharks, dolphins, belugas, carp (the regular boring kind), Giant Pacific Octopus, and hundreds of species of tropical fish.

properties.name: Atlanta History Center
properties.street: 130 W Paces Ferry Rd NW, Atlanta, GA 30305
properties.description: Learn about the history of the 10th largest city in America -including all those times it burned down. The museum also possesses all the artifacts of the Atlanta Cycolrama and Civil War Museum, making it one of the largest Civil War museums in America. The museum isn't just the main building, it's also a garden and farm complex featuring the historic Smith Farm, the neoclassical Swan House mansion, and the Wood Family cabin.

properties.name: Kennedy Space Center Visitor Complex
properties.description: This is THE space museum. Kennedy Space Center is the epicenter of American rocket launching and development. Depending on the day, you can actually see rockets blasting off into space. The museum features the Space Shuttle Atlantis, a complete Saturn V rocket, and a garden full of every type of rocket and capsule America has ever launched. The Kennedy Space Center Bus Tour will take you between the various sections of the space center so you can see everything - including the alligators.

properties.name: Everglades National Park
properties.description: It's not just a swamp, it's a tropical nice swamp full of the wildlife you want to see. It's endless mangroves, alligators, wading birds, crocodiles, and manatees. There's airboat tours so you can see the really good stuff. You can hike around if you like being bitten by mosquitoes.

properties.name: Castillo de San Marcos
properties.street: 11 S Castillo Dr, St. Augustine, FL 32084
properties.description: St. Augustine is the oldest city in the United States, and Castillo de San Marcos is the oldest masonry fort in the United States. The fort saw 251 years of continuous military use between 3 different countries and is best example of spanish fortifications in America.

properties.name: Fort Mantazas National Monument
properties.description: This 1740 Spanish Fort protects the rear entrance to St. Augustine and was built at the inlet to the Matanzas river. It is not longer close to the inlet to the river - the inlet has shifted with time. The small fort is only accessible by tour boat from the National Park Visitor Center.

properties.name: USS Orleck
properties.description: The WW2 era Gearing-class destroyer USS Orleck saw service in Korea and Vietnam and was transfered to the Turkish Navy, only leaving service in 2000. As a result, the interior of the ship is remarkably modern and in good condition. The ship is available for self-guided tour, so you can just wander around.

properties.name: Motorsports Hall of Fame of America
properties.street: 1801 W International Speedway Blvd, Daytona Beach, FL 32114
properties.description: The Daytona International Speedway is the perfect place for a racing museum. Learn about the best drivers that ever were, and see their record-setting racecars.

properties.name: Dry Tortugas National Park
properties.description: This brick fortress is surrounded by pristine coral reefs because it is isolated on the furthest end of the Florida keys. The unfinished Fort Jefferson is the largest masonry structure in the USA. The beaches and fort are nice, but the real draw is the scuba diving and snorkeling to see the sea creatures in an undisturbed environment.  The island is only accessible by boat or seaplane.

properties.name: Fort East Martello Museum
properties.street: 3501 S Roosevelt Blvd, Key West, FL 33040
properties.description: The operators of this already haunted looking Civil War era masonry fort have deliberately tried to make it as creepy as possible by stuffing it with haunted dolls.

properties.name: USCGC Ingham
properties.description: American Coast Guard vessels are the size of the largest warships in other countries navies. The Treasury-class United States Coast Guard Cutter USCGC Ingham sunk U-boats during WW2, and is now a museum ship in the Florida Keys.

properties.name: Fort Zachary Taylor
properties.street: 601 Howard England Way, Key West, FL 33040
properties.description: It's a decaying Civil War era fort on the tropical beaches of Key West, Florida. There's cannons just idily tossed about and iguanas all around - paradise. It's not just the fort and beach that are beautiful, there's scuba diving and snorkeling so you can see the wildlife beneath the sea.

properties.name: John Pennekamp Coral Reef State Park
properties.description: Treal thing worth seeing here is all beneath the sea. Shipwrecks and coral reefs await.

properties.name: Biscayne National Park
properties.description: While the tropical island beaches and beautiful lighthouses are nice - the colorful fish and reefs are nicer. This is your reason to learn to scuba dive or snorkel. The park is mostly underwater or on an island, so you'll need a boat to get there anyway.

properties.name: The Ringling
properties.description: This is THE circus museum. The Ringling is a museum complex consisting of the John and Mable Ringling Museum of Art and The Circus Museum. It's 6 buildings packed full of antiquities and Circus history all built on the grounds of a Circus owner's mansions (yes there's more than one mansion).

properties.name: SS American Victory
properties.description: The SS American Victory is one of the last remaining merchant steamships from WW2 in the United States. The ship is still operational and sails occasionally. Now you can tour it.

properties.name: White Sands Missile Range Museum
properties.street: Building 200, 1 Wsmr P Rt 1, White Sands Missile Range, NM 88002
properties.description: White Sands is the location of the detonation of the Trinity test - the world's first nuclear bomb. It's also the place where the USA tests out its missiles. At the White Sands Missile Range Museum you can see just about every missile ever made by the United States. You will have to pass through a military checkpoint to access this museum - plan ahead.

properties.name: White Sands National Park
properties.description: It's the world's largest gypsum sand dune field, meaning that the sand here is a waving sea of brilliant snow-like white. You can hike on marked trails on the sand dunes if you want - you can even sled down them. Wear sunglasses - the reflected light can hurt your eyes.

properties.name: Carlsbad Caverns National Park
properties.description: This is the other major cave run by the National Park Service - well - 119 caves. Featuring a 750ft descent, the largest cave room by volume in the USA, a mile worth of self guided trails, and a cave that looks stereotypically like you think a cave would look like. Certain areas of the cave require ranger guided tours,the self guided tour is very extensive on its own though. You will need a reservation usually weeks in advance - plan ahead.

properties.name: New Mexico Museum of Space History
properties.description: Featuring The Daisy Track - an-launched sled for safety testing,a mock-up of the X-37B (the USA's top secret robot space shuttle), the International Space Hall of Fame, a garden full of rockets and rocket debris, space suits from various TV series,  and lots and lots of missiles from the nearby White Sands Missile Test Range.

properties.name: Cliffs Amusement Park
properties.description: This small family amusement park in New Mexico has a fast wooden rollercoaster that dives underground and weaves around the entire park. It also has a nice log flume.

properties.name: Anderson Abruzzo Albuquerque International Balloon Museum
properties.street: 9201 Balloon Museum Dr NE, Albuquerque, NM 87113
properties.description: This is THE balloon museum. They have everything on the history of balloons: arctic balloons, high altitude balloons, globe circling balloons, colonial balloons, French balloons, and spy balloons. The entrance is even shaped like a balloon, and they do balloon launches from their front lawn.

properties.name: National Museum of Nuclear Science and History
properties.description: This is THE nuclear museum. New Mexico is home of Los Alamos National Laboratory which developed the first nuclear bomb. This museum will teach you about uranium enrichment, how nuclear reactors are built, nuclear bomb manufacturing, nuclear accidents (and the actual bombs involved in them), and international nuclear weapons. Out back, there's a bunch of nuclear bomb casings, nuclear missiles, a nuclear cannon, a nuclear submarine's sail, and nuclear bombers.

properties.name: New Mexico Bureau of Geology Mineral Museum
properties.description: Have you ever wanted to see every kind of rock there is? Good news, this museum is just 15,000 rocks on row after row of shelves across multiple levels.

properties.name: Petroglyph National Monument
properties.description: Hike through the desert to see 24,000+ Native American drawings on volcanic rock. There are no trails at the visitor's center, so feel free to pick a trail and just start hiking. There's also 4 extinct volcanos on the edge of the park - however they are little more than lumps. Make sure to bring lots and lots of water - this is the desert.

properties.name: Bandalier National Monument
properties.description: The Ancestral Puebloans constructed their homes in the cliffs of a dead volcano. Now you can hike the canyons, badlands, and twisted volcanic rock for yourself.

properties.name: Rio Grande del Norte National Monument
properties.description: The Rio Grande Gorge is like the grand canyon, except surrounded by dead volcanoes. There's also white water rafting. The Wild Rivers Visitor's center puts you closest to the overlooks and trails you likely want to see.

properties.name: Aztec Ruins National Monument
properties.description: These large pre-coloumbian Chacoan ruins structures are some of the best preserved of their kind. At one point this structure had over 400 rooms and was 3 stories high.

properties.name: Chaco Culture National Historical Park
properties.description: Chaco Canyon is full of pre-coloumbian Chacoan ruins, including the massive Pueblo Bonito - the site of a Chacoan city. There's a lot of hiking through scenic desert to do, including through narrow canyons. However, the biggest and best stuff is by the side of the road so you won't have to go very far.

properties.name: Ah-Shi-Sle-Pah Wilderness
properties.description: It's a bunch of alien looking hoodoos in the badlands out in the desert. There is no easy drive to these fancy looking rocks, you'll need to hike for a bit. Bring water, it's the desert.

properties.name: Kasha-Katuwe Tent Rocks National Monument
properties.description: Volcanic ash has formed into a series of conical spires up to 90ft high out in the New Mexico desert. There's also good slot canyons for hiking such as the Cave Loop and Slot Canyon Trails.

properties.name: Bisti/De-Na-Zin Wilderness
properties.description: Eroded badlands have formed some interesting rock formations. The roads are not paved, the trails are loosely marked, and it is the middle of nowhere in the desert - plan accordingly.

properties.name: Makoshika State Park
properties.street: Makoshika State Park, 1301 Snyder St, Glendive, MT 59330
properties.description: If these 11,538-acres of badlands weren't a state park, this would be a national park - that's how good this place is. Makoshika Park Road is the main attraction here, as it saddles the ridge such that badlands surround you on both sides. There are hiking trails down into the badlands themselves if you are feeling ambitious.

properties.name: Glacier National Park
properties.street: Saint Mary Visitor Center, Browning, MT 59417
properties.description: The prarrie meets the tundra right here where glaciers slide down the rocky mountains into glimmering glacial lakes. There's 700 miles of hiking trails, wildlife, 25 glaciers, and waterfalls. Going-To-The-Sun Road snakes through the park so you can enjoy nearly all of it the way America intended. The park gets busy because it's pretty.

properties.name: Kootenai Falls
properties.description: This wide waterfall pours through a richly-colored picturesque canyon in the middle of Kootenai National Forest. You also get to cross a terrifying swinging bridge across the fast-flowing Kootenay River just to get to the overlook.

properties.name: Upper Missouri Breaks National Monument
properties.description: njoy 365,000 acres of plains, cliffs, and rivers where paddle steamers pioneered the frontier. This is one of those 'wander around in the wilderness' type of federal lands with unpaved high-clearance roads such as the missouri Breaks National Back Country Byway.

properties.name: Hill Aerospace Museum
properties.street: 7961 Cottonwood St Building 1955, Hill AFB, UT 84056
properties.description: This aerospace museum features 70+ aircraft across 3 hangars. Including a B1B-Lancer, the double decker C-124C Globemaster II, F-22 Raptor, F-117 Nighthawk, and SR-71C Blackbird.

properties.name: Antelope Island State Park
properties.description: From Antelope island you can get a good view of the mountains, and of the US's largest salt lake. Wild bison herds roam the island, and there are trailheads to the small mountains in the middle of the island.

properties.name: Zion National Park
properties.street: Zion National Park, 1 Zion Park Blvd, Springdale, UT 84767
properties.description: Zion National Park is full of colorful tall vertical walls that close in on either side of you - and you can hike nearly all of it. Highlights include the vertical spine of Angel's Landing, the slot canyons of The Subway and The narrows, the waterfalls of Emerald Pools and Kannara Falls, and Kolob Arch. Make reservations ahead of time - the hikes are popular.

properties.name: Arches National Park
properties.street: Arches National Park Visitor Center, Moab, UT 84532
properties.description: Natural arches are often worth the trip to just see one - this place has 2,000+ set in a fiery red valley. The scenic drive provides good view of some arches - but the most stunning ones you have to hike on trails to get to, such as: Double Arch, Windows, Delicate Arch, Upper Delicate Arch Viewpoint, Sand Dune Arch, Skyline Arch, and Devil's Garden trail. You might need reservations to get onto the road in the park - plan ahead.

properties.name: Canyonlands national Park
properties.street: Island In The Sky Visitor Center, Grand View Point Rd, Moab, UT 84532
properties.description: The Colorado River has created even more spectacular grand canyons. Canyonlands is divided by the confluence of the Colorado River and its tributaries into 4 districts - each is a park in itself: the dazzling views from the cliffs above the canyons at Island In The Sky district, the trails through the spires of The Needles district, the inaccessible backwoods of The Maze district, and the only accessible outside of the park Rivers District.

properties.name: Capitol Reef National Park
properties.street: Capitol Reef National Park Visitor Center, Torrey, UT 84775
properties.description: A 100-mile spine called the Waterpocket Fold stretches through the domes, natural arches, and canyons of this National Park. It's a literal wrinkle in the earth. The park is huge, and is divided into three districts: the Scenic Drive Road in the verdant valley and pink cliffs of the Fruita Historic District, the dirt roads and stunning spires and stacks of Cathedral Valley, and the remote South District.

properties.name: Bryce Canyon National Park
properties.street: Bryce Canyon National Park Visitor Center, UT-63, Bryce Canyon City, UT 84764
properties.description: Imagine if the Grand Canyon was spikey - that's Bryce Canyon. This is the highest concentration of hoodoos anywhere on earth. You can hike down into the canyon if you want, but you can see nearly everything from the viewpoints along Park Road - including the famous Bryce Amphitheater.

properties.name: Cedar Breaks National Monument
properties.description: This is Bryce Canyon National Park's smaller and less popular sibling. It's got beautiful hoodoos in an amphitheater just like Bryce Canyon - except more eroded. You can hike down the cliffs if you want to - but the best views are at the top where you started.

properties.name: Kodachrome Basin State Park
properties.street: 2905 Kodachrome State Park Rd, Canyon Point, UT 84741
properties.description: Kodachrome basin is known for its 67 tall and colorful sand pipes. You can see a lot of this park by driving through it, but the very best can only be seen by hiking.

properties.name: Grand Staircase–Escalante National Monument
properties.description: Different layers of sedimentary rock gradually climb upwards like a staircase over the length of this park. It's a vast landscape of cliffs, canyons, plateaus and badlands reaching between the Grand Canyon and Cedar Breaks. There's lots of canyons to see and hike - the only problem is it's spread out over a large area. For instance, the Burr Trail road is 67 miles long. Highlights include Big Horn Canyon, Escalante River, and Calf Creek trails.

properties.name: Dead Horse Point State Park
properties.street: Dead Horse Point State Park, UT-313, Moab, UT 84532
properties.description: Dead Horse Point State Park overlooks a scenic bend in the river. You can think of it as the state park companion to Canyonlands National Park where you can drive to the bottom of the canyon.

properties.name: Rainbow Bridge National Monument
properties.description: Rainbow Bridge is one of the largest natural bridges in the world - and it looks exactly like a freestanding arch. Unfortunately you can only get to it via boat and hiking from Lake Powell.

properties.name: Natural Bridges National Monument
properties.street: Natural Bridges Rd, Lake Powell, UT 84533
properties.description: Three large natural bridges arch over the canyons of desert landscape. Underneath the overhangs of the canyon lay the ruins of Pueblan cliff dwellings. Just follow Bridge View drive, and you'll see all of the natural bridges.  If you are more ambitious, there are trails that go down into the canyon so you can get close

properties.name: Timpanogos Cave national Monument
properties.street: 2038 E Alpine Lp Rd, American Fork, UT 84003
properties.description: Three caves with sealife like calcite formations are connected by man made tunnels. The caves are only accessible by guided tour - which requires hiking a 1.5 mile trail to the entrance of the caves themselves. Get a reservation - plan ahead.

properties.name: Black Canyon of the Gunnison National Park
properties.description: This 2722ft deep canyon has near vertical walls along its entire narrow length.  The canyon is so narrow and deep that it is constantly in shadow. There are visitor stations and scenic roads along both sides so you can see everything. The guard rails are only waist-high, so don't be stupid.

properties.name: Mesa Verde National Park
properties.description: Mesa Verde preserves 600 pre-coloumbian cliff dwellings and 5000 archaelogical sites. You can see dwelling after dwelling in stop after stop as you follow the roads atop the mesa. You can hike down into the canyons and up to some of the cliff housings when rangers are present.

properties.name: Rocky Mountain National Park
properties.description: 12,000ft tall mountains, lakes, glaciers, and waterfalls. Because this is America, you can drive across the mountains via Trail Ridge Road and Old Fall River Road. Or you can hike if you like exercise - remember you are at a high altitude so it's harder than it seems.

properties.name: Grand Teton National Park
properties.description: It's really big and pretty snowy mountains (13,775ft) next to lakes. There's some lakes you can drive next to, but to actually experience the mountains, waterfalls, and canyons you need to go hiking - and the trails are steep.

properties.name: Pinnacles National Park
properties.description: Eroded volcanic pinnacles from an exinct volcano and canyons are yours to explore through hiking and climbing.  The park is divided into the popular east side, and the remote hiking oriented west side. Popular hikes include Bear Gulch Reservoir for the canyons, and High Peaks for the pinnacles.

properties.name: Yosemite National Park
properties.description: a 3500ft glacial valley with sheer cliffs, 2500ft waterfalls, and 250ft Giant Sequoia. There are too many beautiful parts of this park to list. It's really pretty, really busy, and you can hike all of it. Plan ahead.

properties.name: Joshua Tree National Park
properties.description: This park is full of mountains, wind shaped rocks, and a forest of the wacky desert plant that is the Joshua Tree. It's the desert, so don't attempt any big hikes in the summer. Popular hikes include the crowded Skull Rock and Jumbo Rocks; and the less busy Wonderland of Rocks, Arch Rock, Hidden Valley, and Keyes View. There's abandoned gold mines if you are up for longer treks - and

properties.name: La Brea Tar Pits and Museum
properties.description: There's just lakes of oil in the middle of Los Angeles where prehistoric creatures died. Now you can see their bones!

properties.name: Academy Museum of Motion Pictures
properties.street: LACMA West, 6067 Wilshire Blvd, Los Angeles, CA 90036
properties.description: All the costumes and props from your favorite movies tend to end up here. You can also watch movies here.

properties.name: Petersen Automotive Museum
properties.description: It's a car museum, but only the really expensive cars -like Saddam Hussein's mercedes.

properties.name: California Science Center
properties.street: 700 Exposition Park Dr, Los Angeles, CA 90037
properties.description: The Space Shuttle Endeavour lives here in full-stack launch position with the booster and fuel tank. There's also some space capsules, space probe replicas, and a few airplanes. To top it off there is a giant animatronic in the middle of a vivisection that talks to you.

properties.name: The Getty Center
properties.street: 1200 Getty Center Dr, Los Angeles, CA 90049
properties.description: The richest art institution in the world would like you to see how much art they own - for free. It's 120,000 pieces of art spread across six buildings in the complex.

properties.name: American Military Museum
properties.street: 1918 Rosemead Blvd, South El Monte, CA 91733
properties.description: 180+ Military Vehicles packed together next to a crowdless junkyard in the dry California heat. If you ever just wanted to stare at the equivalent of a used-car lot full of military vehicles in an eerily empty environment - this is the place. Including LVT-4 landing vehicles, and a Vietnam river boat.

properties.name: Sequoia National Park
properties.description: America has the biggest and most beautiful trees. Giant Sequoias can grow up to 250ft tall with 20ft diameter trunks - that's larger than most European houses. The trees are so big you can and do literally drive through a tree on the park roads.   Oh the park is also in a stunningly beautiful canyon - make sure to check out the Moro Rock Trail. There's hiking, rock climbing, and a road if you just want to drive through.

properties.name: USS Iowa Museum
properties.street: 250 S Harbor Blvd, San Pedro, CA 90731
properties.country: 250 S Harbor Blvd, San Pedro, CA 90731
properties.description: It's the lead ship of the largest class of battleships the United States has ever built. The USS Iowa served in WW2, Korea, and during the Cold War. Now you can wander around this massive ship in sunny LA.

properties.name: SS Lane Victory
properties.street: Berth 52, 2400 Miner St, San Pedro, CA 90731
properties.description: Another one of the few afloat survivors of the 1940s merchant marine. SS Lane Victory was a mass produced Victory-ship. The ship  served in WW2, Korea, and Vietnam moving military supplies and civilians. Now the ship's cargo holds are a museum you can roam about in.

properties.name: Southern California Railway Museum
properties.description: Almost all of LA's streetcars from its once extensive mass transit system have ended up at this museum. See 28 types of streetcars and a couple of trains.

properties.name: Kings Canyons National Park
properties.description: Kings Canyon is a valley full of the world's largest trees, waterfalls, roaring rivers, and scenic mountainside. You can see most of what you want to see from the scenic drive - however there are good hikes at Zumwalt Meadow loop, Roaring River Falls, and Mist Falls. This park is busy - it's right next to Sequoia National Park.

properties.name: Devils Postpile National Monument
properties.description: The cliff of hexagonal columns look almost deliberately constructed - but they're just volcanic basaltic formations. If Hexagons aren't enough to excite you, there's also the 101ft Rainbow Falls, a scenic road loop, and hiking everywhere you could want.

properties.name: Hot Creek Geologic Site
properties.street: Hot Creek Hatchery Rd, Mammoth Lakes, CA 93546
properties.description: Inside of Inyo National Forest, Hot Creek literally boils, and so do the nearby geysers, springs, and fumaroles. You cannot go inside the water - you can see everything from the viewpoints along the road anyway.

properties.name: Hearst Castle
properties.street: 750 Hearst Castle Rd, San Simeon, CA 93452
properties.description: William Randolph Hearst was a media tycoon within his time and used his influence to try and influence national politics - something that I'm sure has never happened since. He also built this incredibly lavish mansion stuffed full of antiquities. This mansion is literally built out of pieces of historical architecture shipped in from Europe.

properties.name: Redwood National and State Parks
properties.street: Newton B. Drury Scenic Pkwy, Orick, CA 95555
properties.description: The Federal Government and California have teamed up to the protect the temperate rainforest of the California Redwood - the tallest trees in the world. There's lakes, rivers, and coastline to hike through, popular hikes include: Fern Canyon  - a canyon covered in greenery (you need a reservation), Tall Trees Grove (permit required), Jedidiah Smith Trail, and Lady Bird Johnson Trail.

properties.name: Burney Falls
properties.description: Burney Falls emerges from a creek and springs and descends a bowl shaped 129ft drop as a series of streams. The trails here at McArthur–Burney Falls Memorial State Park loop to the bottom of the falls and up into the hills.

properties.name: Lassen Volcanic National Park
properties.description: Every type of volcano is found here at the southernmost volcanos in the United States. Featuring plug dome volcanoes, shield volcanoes, cinder cone volcanoes, stratovolcanoes, lava beds, boiling mud pots, fumaroles, hotsprings, thermal vents, and waterfalls. Locations you have to see include the bubbling Bumpass Hell, the steaming Sulphur Works, and the lavabeds and painted dunes of Cinder Cone. There's a lot of hiking to do, but there's a lot accessible from the roadway.

properties.name: Palm Springs Aerial Tramway
properties.description: The Palm Springs Aerial Tramway is the only realistic way for non-experienced climbers to reach the 10,834ft views of Mount San Jacinto State Park. The tramway is a sight in itself, it travels 2.5 miles up a jagged rocky canyon to a luxury villa at the top. Once you get up there, there's some scenic hikes.

properties.name: Royal Gorge Bridge and Park
properties.description: The Royal Gorge Bridge was the tallest bridge in the world from 1929-2001 and spans the narrow and deep Royal Gorge. Remarkably, despite the dangerous canyon walls and flooding river, there is a rail line at the bottom of this gorge. You can cross the gorge by pedestrian bridge or gondola, and look out over the side at the numerous viewpoints.

properties.name: Pikes Peak
properties.street: 101 El Paso Blvd, Manitou Springs, CO 80829
properties.description: Pikes Peach dominates the surrounding mountains with its 14,115ft height - which is exactly why America built a road to the top so you can experience the views without leaving your car. There's also a train that will take you to the top.

properties.name: Garden of the Gods
properties.street: 1423-1427 Juniper Way Loop, Colorado Springs, CO 80904
properties.description: Sharp red rock fins jut out of the green landscape at the Garden of the Gods in Colorado. You can walk around most of the formations on the walking trails. You can drive by it on Juniper Way Loop

properties.name: Manitou Cliff Dwellings
properties.description: 1907 Tourist promoters built a replica of Puebloan Cliff dwellings out of actual historical  cliff dwelling materials from other sites. Unlike the genuine cliff dwellings at Mesa Verde, these you can actually walk around in.

properties.name: Western Museum of Mining and Industry
properties.street: 225 North Gate Blvd, Colorado Springs, CO 80921
properties.description: It's 27 acres of antique mining equipment - and most of it still runs. Including a steam shovel, a stamp mill, the Chilean Rescue pod used to rescue miners from a deep underground mine in Chile,

properties.name: May Natural History Museum
properties.street: 710 Rock Creek Canyon Rd, Colorado Springs, CO 80926
properties.description: Row after row of 7,000 terrifyingly large insects pinned for display. There's even the world's largest statue of a beetle outside.

properties.name: Castlewood Canyon State Park
properties.description: Stroll through the corpse of a 1890 masonry dam that collapsed and flooded Denver in 1933. The 2628 acre canyon also features nice looking rock formations that you can hike through.

properties.name: Roxborough State Park
properties.description: Angular red sandstone slabs of rock portrude from the landscape like a slab of arrowheads. You can hike on part of the east side, but the west side is a subdivision, and the north side is a golf course.

properties.name: Mile High Comics - Jason Street Mega Store
properties.description: It's basically comic book Costco. 45,000sqft of15 million comics books..

properties.name: Casa Bonita
properties.description: "The Disneyland of Mexican Restaurants". Featuring indoor cliff divers, a western town with actors, a haunted tunnel, mariachi bands, and magic and puppet shows, . Casa Bonita was featured in an episode of the cartoon series South Park, and is now owned by the creators of South Park. As a result, its popularity has skyrocketed, and reservations are required months in advance.

properties.name: Colorado Railroad Museum
properties.description: See how railroading gets done in the mountains. Most of the trains still work. Featuring historical locomotives from the Pikes Peak Railway, Galloping Goose, and various historical mountain trains. There's also a nice model train in the basement that runs on quarters.

properties.name: Eldorado Canyon State Park
properties.description: That's right - it's another gorgeous canyon full of beautiful hiking in Colorado. There's rock climbing, river rapids, the ruins of a hotel, and 11 miles of trails. Hike to the top of the canyon at the Rattlesnake Gulch Trail (featuring actual Rattlesnakes), or take in the views from afar at the Walker Ranch Loop Trail.  On the weekends you will need a reservation - it gets busy, and the parking lot is small - so plan ahead.

properties.name: Colorado Railroad Railroad Museum
properties.description: It's a 5500sqft HO layout that takes the HO scale trains an hour to complete. There's multiple train cars inside the building if that's enough not enough for you.

properties.name: Glenwood Caverns Adventure Park
properties.street: 51000 Two Rivers Plaza Road, Glenwood Springs, CO 81601
properties.description: It's an amusement park build on top of a mountain with a dramatic view of the valley below. Featuring a swing that swings you over the edge, a drop tower that sends you plummeting down a mineshaft, and an alpine coaster that rides down the mountainside. There's also some pretty caves.

properties.name: Hanging Lake Park
properties.description: Waterfalls pour out of a vertical cliffside into a lake on top of a mountain. Part of the White River National Forest. Only accessible by trail.

properties.name: Colorado National Monument
properties.description: The western section of Colorado looks more like the Grand Canyon than the Rockies. The formations at Monument canyon are the star of this park. Featuring tall spires, hoodoos, and deep canyons. Most of the park can be seen from Rim Rock Drive, however you can hike on trails to descend into the canyon itself.

properties.name: Canyon of the Ancients National Monument
properties.description: Think of this as the companion national monument to Mesa Verde National Park. This national monument preserves pre-columbian Puebloan ruins spread across 176,000acres. This includes the Lowey Puebleo and its 47ft diameter kiva, the Painted Hand pueblo on the edge of a cliff, and the small cliff dwelling of the Sand Canyon pueblo. You are going to have to do a small amount of hiking to get to each of the sites from the roadway.

properties.name: Box Canyon (Colorado)
properties.description: A mining camp was threaded through a tight box canyon with a 285ft waterfall. Now you can walk the metal trail that winds through the canyon and stare down the steep and narrow gorge. It's just a short hike from Box Canon Falls park.

properties.name: Underground Mining Museum
properties.description: The museum itself is completely underground, but you can see the rotting ruins of the abandoned mine high in the cliffs of the shadow valley above you.

properties.name: Last Chance Mine
properties.street: 504 Last Chance Mine Rd, Creede, CO 81130
properties.description: This silver mine is terrifying. Everything in your body screams you are about to get lost, dragged into the shadows, or fall down a crevice. Go on a private tour for maximum effect.

properties.name: Dinosaur National Monument
properties.description: See actual dinosaur fossils embedded into the rock. Oh and there's also some massive canyons with river rafting. See the fossials at the Quarry Exhibit Hall, the bends of the canyon at Harper's Corner, and the steep spine and riverbend at Echo Park (high-clearance 4-wheel drive vehicles only).

properties.name: National Museum of Military Vehicles
properties.description: This is THE land military vehicle museum. 500+ military vehicles hoarded by Dan Starks are now the centerpiece of this 160,000 sqft attraction. There's also a vault full of guns.
